title: Scheduling Pods with dynamic resources and using the Pod `.spec.nodeName` field fails
description:
### What happened?

The combination of using the Pod spec nodeName field with the `DynamicResources` scheduler plugin (currently feature-gated) doesn't work. No surprise really as the nodeName field effective bypasses the `DynamicResources` scheduler plugin running, and something rather clever would need to be invented to make things to work. But this is still a bit of a regression compared to the old device plugin model which doesn't have a similar limitation.  @pohly as the author of the dynamic resources feature can explain what could maybe be created to fix this.

Granted, forcing scheduling even with a device plugin resource may or may not succeed at the node level depending on the availability of said plugin resources at the node, but with dynamic resources the failure seems to be currently guaranteed.

The use-case for this is such that the Kubernetes scheduler is effectively being preceded by some other scheduler which runs earlier (say, some HPC framework) which is giving the Pods the node names and somehow knows that there will be enough resources, and then the workloads ought to land in the specified node and the container related work is then handled normally from there on. So basically Kubernetes wouldn't do much in terms of scheduling, but takes over from there.

### What did you expect to happen?

TBH I expected it to fail and it did. The resource claims won't work, since the scheduler plugin isn't getting a chance to do its thing.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Just use DRA with Pod spec nodeName field, one needs a DRA driver obviously.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>
Working with dynamic-resource-allocation branch from @pohly which recently got merged to the coming 1.26 release

comments.text:
One possible solution would be to have a new controller which specifically watches for pods in this state (nodeName set and reference claims). That controller then must trigger delayed allocation (if needed) by creating a PodScheduling object with selectedNode set. After allocation it must add the pod to the reservedFor list.

kubelet will immediately try to run the pod once it sees it because of the nodeName field. It will refuse to run it until eventually all claims are allocated and reserved.

Obviously using a scheduler which is not aware of dynamic resources is problematic. There is no guarantee that the chosen node even has the hardware that is needed for the pod and that it isn't in use. It would be good to hear from whoever has this use case whether the solution outlined above would work in practice.

The alternative is to build support for dynamic resource allocation into that other scheduler.
Should this be a beta blocker? Or we just want to mark this an unsupported behavior long-term?

My approach: provide a sample / “contrib” implementation of a restriction that prohibits specifying `.spec.nodeName` - other than by binding the Pod - for a Pod that also requests dynamic resources.

If ValidatingAdmissionPolicy gains a way to restrict this, we can provide a contrib ValidatingAdmissionPolicy as well, and recommend that tools for managing cluster lifecycle put that in place.

That'd be enough to move to beta. IMO.

> Should this be a beta blocker?

I'm not sure whether it needs to be a blocker, but my intention is to work on this soonish - definitely before beta.
I intend to support this instead of prohibiting it.
It sounds like it could be a non-trivial change to the design. Once you have something, please send a PR to the KEP.

title: kube-apiserver doesn't clean up OpenAPI properly after deleting an APIService/CRD
description:
### What happened?

I noticed some odd behaviors/logs after deleting APIServices and CRDs.

First, only CRDs were removed from the response of `/openapi/v3` and APIServices were not removed. Not only the root path, the APIService's specific paths were also available, e.g. `/openapi/v3/apis/foo.bar.com/v1alpha1`, as if they were not deleted.

Second, there were some confusing logs in kube-apiserver, indicating it failed to do some cleanup, and every failure was duplicated once:
```
E0822 15:24:36.314675       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1alpha1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.314705       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1alpha1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.316316       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1beta1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
E0822 15:24:36.317664       1 controller.go:159] removing "v1beta1.crd.antrea.io" from AggregationController failed with: resource not found
```

After checking the code, I found the above observations were caused by the same code in kube-apiserver which didn't handle the removal of APIService correctly:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/aa8cb97f65fe1d24e96eda129337d86109615570/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/apiserver.go#L563-L568

Basically apiserver was calling wrong AggregationController when removing APIService, which caused OpenAPI v3 not cleaned up and the duplicate errors. There was another issue in v2 AggregationController which caused the error. 

Besides, just correcting L567 didn't fix the problem totally, there were some other issues in the implementation.

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-apiserver should clean up OpenAPI correctly, shoud not generate confusing errors.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Install some APIServices and CRDs and remove all of them, then check the response of "/openapi/v3" and kube-apiserver logs.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: kube-proxy: -v command line flag reset by --config file
description:
### What happened?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117800 introduced configuration of additional logging aspects (e.g. format) through command line flags and config file. This was merged for Kubernetes 1.28.

Now the following invocation doesn't work as expected when the config file doesn't configure logging:
```
kube-proxy -- --config kube-proxy.conf -v=4
```

### What did you expect to happen?

It should run with verbosity 4. Instead it runs with verbosity 0, from the config.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run with this config file:
```
apiVersion: kubeproxy.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: KubeProxyConfiguration
```

comments.text:
The problem is caused by this line:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f0dcf0614036d8c3cd1c9f3b3cf8df4bb1d8e44e/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L250

At that point, `o.config.Logging.Verbosity` is 4 (from the command line flag), and then it gets overwritten with `c.Verbosity` == 0.

The normal approach would be:
- set up config with defaults
- modify config through flags
- modify config further by parsing a config file into it.

Can kube-proxy do this? It has the downside that a config file can only overwrite fields if they are in the file. A config field doesn't get reset to defaults just by parsing the file.
it looks like kube-proxy special-cases the `processHostnameOverrideFlag` to let a flag override config... can/should it do the same thing for verbosity? are there any other flags like this?

> The normal approach would be:
> 
> * set up config with defaults
> * modify config through flags
> * modify config further by parsing a config file into it.

I don't think that's the normal approach... it's more normal to make flags and config file mutually exclusive. That's difficult for things which started as flags and moved into config

Hey folks, v1.28  Bug Triage Lead here 👋🏼 

Just wanted to know if this is already tracked by SIG leads and someone already working actively fixing it and set a priority?

> I don't think that's the normal approach...

Perhaps I should have said "this is how component-base/logs was meant to be used". Somehow it worked for kubelet.

Here's my preliminary solution: [REDACTED]

It needs more testing, but I wanted to share it early because I am running out of time today.

it is @furkatgofurov7 , I can take over Patrick's work in case is needed

It would be nice if the logs API could distinguish between `setting it to 0` and `not setting it`, how about make `verbosity` to a pointer?  But this change is supposed to be a breaking change, I'm not sure of the scope of the impact.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e6218f3d3bede036b2d67a4349dd761aac06ae97/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1/types.go#L53

For `kube-proxy` side, if set `--config` and `command flags` at the same time, should the command flag override the config file or warn it and be discarded?  I think it should be overridden.

title: the preemption happens even when PreFilter returns UnschedulableAndUnresolvable
description:
When PreFilter returns UnschedulableAndUnresolvable, we don't need to run the preemption, but currently we run.
This unexpected preemption could cause errors from the preemption by trying to read non-exist PreFilter data.

As @Huang-Wei pointed out ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119770#issuecomment-1666418637)), actually we didn't run the preemption in such cases in the past versions, but https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/110894 introduced this bug.

title: CronJob gets stuck when jobs quota is reached
description:
### What happened?

We (in Booking.com) run CronJobs in Kubernetes clusters with ResourceQuota's defined. When quota for # of jobs is reached we observed that CronJobs:
1. stop scheduling new jobs (because quota is reached),
2. don't clean the old jobs (despite # of jobs > history allows and the fact that it would unblock the CronJob new Jobs). 

The only way to progress is to remove enough Jobs to make room for a new Job in namespace quota. When we do that manually, the CronJob kicks in.

The workaround we found around the internet is to specify `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` for the job template. But it's not ideal as it's not a history-based limit, but a time-based limit, and often you want to have the last N jobs to be around for debugging.

### What did you expect to happen?

When jobs quota is reached and # of cronjob jobs exceeds specified the history limit, these jobs are deleted giving room for new jobs to run.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: job-quota
  namespace: default
spec:
  hard:
    count/jobs.batch: "1"
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: hello-world-cronjob
spec:
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 0
  schedule: "* * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: hello-world
              image: bash
              command: ["bash", "-c", "sleep 80"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

1. Wait for a first Job to be created (which will fill up the jobs quota) at X minute.
2. A job for X + 1 will fail to be created (because quota won't allow, and X job is still running).
3. All future attempts to create a new job by the controller will fail (check `kubectl get events --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail`, you'll see re-occuring `Error creating job: jobs.batch "hello-world-cronjob-28187648" is forbidden: exceeded quota: job-quota, requested: count/jobs.batch=1, used: count/jobs.batch=1, limited: count/jobs.batch=1`).
4. The first job will never be cleaned (although it will be eligible, since history is 0).

### Anything else we need to know?

Looks like the problem was introduced in the `cronjob_controllerv2.go` implementation: if `jm.syncCronJob` returned an error, we return from the function and never invoke `jm.cleanupFinishedJobs`.:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controllerv2.go#L199-L213

In the old `cronjob_controller.go` implementation this was not the case:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0f77da5bd4809927e15d1658fb4aa8f13ad890a5/pkg/controller/cronjob/cronjob_controller.go#L137-L138

title: sched: CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins not always injected into cycleState
description:
### What happened?

In k8s 1.27, scheduler introduced a new "short circuit" semantics in PreFilter to bypass a Pod quickly. A change introduced here is it relies on that plugin to be stored in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins`, which makes sense as what it was explained [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/114125/files#r1062646736).

However, the `SkipFilterPlugins` info, although is populated upon each plugin's PreFilter invocation, is not injected into `CycleState` when some PreFilter returns unschedulable:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L655-L661

So think about this workflow:

- pluginA returns Skip in its PreFilter
- pluginB return Unschedulable in its PreFilter
- note: pluginA is not included in `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` due to aforementioned bug
- a Pod is claimed as unschedulable (failed by pluginB)
- during PostFilter, it's **supposed** to bypass pluginA's PreEnqueueExtension's AddPod/RemovePod, but it doesn't
- calling a "skipped" Plugin's AddPod/RemovePod during preemption, sometimes will abort the whole preemption as the logic tries to read info from cycleState, and some plugin's "skip" version doesn't fill cycleState properly, e.g., InterPodAffinity (skip immediately w/o write preFilterStateKey).

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L257-L262

### What did you expect to happen?

Short circuiting using Skip is fine, but `CycleState.SkipFilterPlugins` should injected properly at all cases.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Described in the workflow above.

It's firstly captured in an out-of-tree PostFilter plugin: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/scheduler-plugins/pull/608#issuecomment-1665855370, but can also happen in in-tree plugins.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

Among in-tree plugins, 3 plugins employ non-nil `PreFilterExtensions` and may return Skip in their PreFilter() implementation w/o writing `preFilterStateKey` to cycleState, while return error immediately if `preFilterStateKey` is missing in their Add/RemovePod() functions.

title: CEL Estimated cost incorrect for lowerAscii
description:
### What happened?

Creating a CRD with a case-insensitive uniqueness check and appropriate maxLength/maxItems limits should be allowed:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: uniquetests.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                headers:
                  type: array
                  maxItems: 1
                  x-kubernetes-validations:
                    - rule: "self.all(item1, self.exists_one(item2, item1.name.lowerAscii() == item2.name.lowerAscii()))"
                  items:
                    type: object
                    properties:
                      name:
                        maxLength: 1
                        type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: uniquetests
    singular: uniquetest
    kind: UniqueTest
```

But I got:

```
kubectl apply -f unique.yaml
The CustomResourceDefinition "uniquetests.stable.example.com" is invalid: 
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[headers].x-kubernetes-validations[0].rule: Forbidden: estimated rule cost exceeds budget by factor of more than 100x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength where arrays, maps, and strings are declared)
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.properties[spec].properties[headers].x-kubernetes-validations[0].rule: Forbidden: contributed to estimated rule cost total exceeding cost limit for entire OpenAPIv3 schema
* spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema: Forbidden: x-kubernetes-validations estimated rule cost total for entire OpenAPIv3 schema exceeds budget by factor of more than 100x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength where arrays, maps, and strings are declared)
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the estimated cost to be very low with maxItems=1 and maxLength=1.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This also exceeds the estimated cost limit, suggesting the problem is unrelated to the array:

```yaml
 x-kubernetes-validations:                                                                                        
  - rule: "self[0].name.lowerAscii() == self[0].name.lowerAscii()"
```

But this is valid (estimated cost is under the limit):

```yaml
x-kubernetes-validations:                                                                                        
  - rule: "self.all(item1, self.exists_one(item2, item1.name == item2.name))"
```

Which suggests that the estimated cost system is not handling `lowerAscii` correctly.  The estimated cost of `lowerAscii` should be a function of the input string length (which in this case has a max length of 1), and, for purposes of subsequent cost calculations, the resulting value of `lowerAscii` should be known by the estimated cost system to be the same length as the input string.



### Anything else we need to know?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/2c6c4566eff972d6c1320b5f8ad795f88c822d09/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/library/cost.go#L119 is where the estimated cost of lowerAscii is handled. Just glancing at the code I don't see an obvious problem.

title: PodDisruptionBudget with an empty selector `{}` being honored incorrectly
description:
### What happened?

`PodDisruptionBudget` with an empty selector `{}` selects all the pods as expected.
But, during the `drain` /`eviction`, the pdb is not being honored correctly i.e. all the pods are getting evicted.

This issue is only observed with the empty selector and works as expected if a valid label selector is provided that selects all the pods in a namespace.

### What did you expect to happen?

When an empty selector `{}` is provided in the `PodDisruptionBudget`'s spec, the created `PodDisruptionBudget` needs to be honored by not evicting all the pods during the `drain/eviction` api call

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a simple busybox deployment with 3 replicas on a local cluster (or any cluster)
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: busybox
  name: busybox
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busybox
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 25%
      maxUnavailable: 25%
    type: RollingUpdate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busybox
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: busybox
        name: busybox
        command: ["sleep", "1000"]
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
      restartPolicy: Always
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30

```
- Create a pdb object with an `empty` selector `{}`

title: Service `status.loadBalancer.ingress` can be set when `type` != `LoadBalancer`
description:
xref 119454

I think this may be one of the few cases where we can actually change the behavior in a "breaking" way.

User creates service with `.type=ClusterIP`, `.status.loadBalancer` is empty
Controller or user updates the status subresource, sets `.spec.loadBalancer.ingress[].ip` (not wiped or validated, should be)
User updates `service spec` in any way, `.staus.loadBalancer` is wiped

It's clear that the `.status.loadBalancer` is not meant to be set when `.type` is not "LoadBalancer".

The question is:

1) Fail validation?
2) Silently discard the value?
3) Warn and then discard the value?
4) Just warn and leave it.

Because we allowed it in the past, but it is so volatile, I lean towards 3.

@aojea and @khenidak - the people most familair with this type.

Edit: PrepareForUpdate() runs before warnings.  So:

(1) is easy
(2) is easy
(4) is slightly less easy than (2)
(3) is slightly less easy than (4)

title: Namespace stuck in Terminating when deleted if ApiService doesn't implement Aggregated Discovery
description:
### What happened?

We implement a manual `APIService` API Extension in [Agones](https://github.com/googleforgames/agones).

Definition:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/install/helm/agones/templates/service/allocation.yaml

Code for handling web requests:
https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/pkg/util/apiserver/apiserver.go

The code is extremely lightweight as we only have no need for storage, and only accept CREATE requests at this time.

This issue was first reported by one of our users in May, but we only were able to reproduce it ourselves once we were on 1.27.x: https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/issues/3172

Testing on Kubernetes 1.27.x we noticed that when attempting to delete Namespaces, they would get stuck in termination with the following description:

```
❯ kubectl describe ns 1690585578
Name:         1690585578
Labels:       kubernetes.io/metadata.name=1690585578
              owner=e2e-test
Annotations:  <none>
Status:       Terminating
Conditions:
  Type                                         Status  LastTransitionTime               Reason                  Message
  ----                                         ------  ------------------               ------                  -------
  NamespaceDeletionDiscoveryFailure            True    Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:07:44 -0700  DiscoveryFailed         Discovery failed for some groups, 1 failing: unable to retrieve the complete list of server APIs: allocation.agones.dev/v1: stale GroupVersion discovery: allocation.agones.dev/v1
  NamespaceDeletionGroupVersionParsingFailure  False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:07:46 -0700  ParsedGroupVersions     All legacy kube types successfully parsed
  NamespaceDeletionContentFailure              False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentDeleted          All content successfully deleted, may be waiting on finalization
  NamespaceContentRemaining                    False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentRemoved          All content successfully removed
  NamespaceFinalizersRemaining                 False   Fri, 28 Jul 2023 16:08:56 -0700  ContentHasNoFinalizers  All content-preserving finalizers finished
```

So far, I've not found a way to delete the Namespace.

Looking through the log for the webserver, i can see requests for `/apis` and the new Aggregated Discovery feature (`Accept:  "application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList"`), but we return a 404 to that response, since it's not implemented.

Looking through the code I can find (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.3/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/handler_discovery.go) it seems that any response other than `http.StatusOK` would result in this issue -- which is breaking backward compatibility within `APIService` to assume that this API surface is implemented in some way.

### What did you expect to happen?

Namespaces would terminate as per normal.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install Agones on a cluster (https://agones.dev/site/docs/installation/install-agones/)
2. `kubectl create ns foo`
3. `kubectl delete ns foo`
4. Watch as the ns gets stuck in Terminating.


### Anything else we need to know?

If I had a magic wand, I'd love a reference of all the API's that get called against an APIService and what their expected results should be.

So far it's a combo of using `kubectl proxy` and looking at the k8s API responses, crawling through code, and reading apiserver logs to try and reverse engineer this work.

Will edit this comment as we go, but just writing down some useful notes:

- agones should support the `/apis` endpoint: https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/blob/main/pkg/util/apiserver/apiserver.go#L130 so it's weird that a 404 is required
- Aggregated Discovery is fully backwards compatible with previous versions. A fallback https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.3/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/handler_discovery.go#L231-L233 is implemented so not supporting aggregated discovery on an APIService will fall back to the old behavior (without the `Accept:  "application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList"` accept header)
- The issue brought up https://github.com/googleforgames/agones/issues/3172 is on v1.26.5 in which aggregated discovery is disabled (only enabled for 1.27+)

> * Aggregated Discovery is fully backwards compatible with previous versions. A fallback https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.3/staging/src/k8s.io/kube-aggregator/pkg/apiserver/handler_discovery.go#L231-L233 is implemented so not supporting aggregated discovery on an APIService will fall back to the old behavior (without the `Accept:  "application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList"` accept header)

That assumes the aggregated server is paying attention to the Accept header, and will respond with a NotAcceptable status code if it doesn't support aggregated discovery... that may or may not be true... ways we could make that stronger / more compatible:
1. double check the response content-type
2. send a single request to `/apis` that indicates it accepts BOTH `application/json` and `application/json;g=apidiscovery.k8s.io;v=v2beta1;as=APIGroupDiscoveryList`, and use the content-type in the returned data to decide whether to go down the aggregated or normal discovery path


 ideally, it would make a single request that indicated it accepted

Thanks to an offline chat with @Jefftree - can confirm that returning `HTTP: 406` from `/apis` resolved the issue!

Long term we'll look at implementing Aggregate Discovery, but this at least gets us past the initial hurdle. Thanks for the support!

> Thanks to an offline chat with @Jefftree - can confirm that returning `HTTP: 406` from `/apis` resolved the issue!

to be clear, this is returning a 406 to requests that don't accept `application/json`, right?

ah, right... the non-aggregated discovery calls directly to `/apis/$group/$version`

@Jefftree to be actually compatible, I think the "success case" for aggregated discovery should check that the status code is `200` and the returned content is actually aggregated discovery json, and if either of those are false, it should fall back to non-aggregated discovery.

> ah, right... the non-aggregated discovery calls directly to `/apis/$group/$version`
> 
> @Jefftree to be actually compatible, I think the "success case" for aggregated discovery should check that the status code is `200` and the returned content-type is aggregated discovery json, and if either of those are false, it should fall back to non-aggregated discovery.

title: api: Finalizer name format is not enforced for custom resources
description:
### What happened?

A client is allowed to add custom finalizers to Custom Resources with a finalizer name that's not fully qualified (e.g. `example` or `example.com`).

However they're prevented from doing the same on builtin resource types, returning the following error:

    Invalid value: "finalizers.compute.linkedin.com": name is neither a standard finalizer name nor is it fully qualified

### What did you expect to happen?

Per [Custom Resource Definition docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#finalizers:~:text=Identifiers%20of%20custom%20finalizers%20consist%20of%20a%20domain%20name%2C%20a%20forward%20slash%20and%20the%20name%20of%20the%20finalizer), custom finalizer names are expected to be in format "consist of a domain name, a forward slash and the name of the finalizer" (e.g. `foo.bar/name`).

Therefore, I expected the enforcement to be the same for CRs and builtin types.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. have a custom resource on the cluster
2. `kubectl edit` it to add `finalizers: [example.com]`
3. observe the edit does not fail
4. do the same on a builtin resource (e.g. Namespace or Pod), observe it fails

title: API: ResourceRequirements usage in Container and PVC
description:
### What happened?

The same ResourceRequirements struct is used in two only loosely related entities (Container and PersistentVolumeClaim). Extending ResourceRequirements for dynamic resource requirement had the unintended effect that the new `Claims` field also became available in a PersistentVolumeClaim.

title: VolumeZone scheduling plugin should handle csi migration
description:
### What happened?

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268, we discovered that our plan for eventually removing the [VolumeZone](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumezone) scheduling plugin when CSI migration is GA is not possible because the plugin also applies to non-migratable volume types.

However, if we leave the plugin as is, then even migratable PVs will be broken if we remove beta topology labels from Nodes in the future. This is because the plugin does not have any handling for migrated volumes.

### What did you expect to happen?

I suggest we add CSI migration handling to the VolumeZone plugin. I think we just need to detect if the volume is migrated, and if so, skip the VolumeZone processing. For migrated volumes, we translate `PV.Labels` into `PV.NodeAffinity` so they end up getting processed by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

In a cluster with csi migration for a specific intree volume type enabled,
1. create an intree PV with beta topology labels
2. remove the beta topology label from a node
3. try to schedule a pod using that pv

And you think we can translate `PV.Labels` into `PV.NodeAffinity` in volume_zone during `PreFilter`(maybe), and update this pv so that in `Filter` stage, `volumebinding` can `CheckNodeAffinity`, so we don't have compare Topology labels in `volume_zone`.

My question is:
>  For migrated volumes, we translate PV.Labels into PV.NodeAffinity

Can't we just translate this for all pvs? Why do we need to detect if the volume is migrated? What's the difference between a migrated pv and a non-migratable pv in this scenario?

> Can't we just translate this for all pvs? Why do we need to detect if the volume is migrated? What's the difference between a migrated pv and a non-migratable pv in this scenario?

I think this is also another alternative solution that could also work, but from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/114268#issuecomment-1337414393, it may not scalable to do an automatic migration for all the different APIs and controllers that use the node labels. The main difference with CSI migration, is we have a good idea of all the different components that would be impacted and also have reasonable control over those components.

> I think we just need to detect if the volume is migrated, and if so, skip the VolumeZone processing. For migrated volumes, we translate PV.Labels into PV.NodeAffinity so they end up getting processed by the [VolumeBinding](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/tree/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding) plugin.

A few more questions😂

Will the volumes be migrated before we take a pod off the scheduler queue? If so, how can I detect this. Currently I find a function `IsPVMigratable` in `csi-translation-lib`, but nothing like  `IsPVMigrated`.

2.  > For migrated volumes, we translate PV.Labels into PV.NodeAffinity

Is this translation  done in `volume_zone` plugin or before scheduling?

3.  I think currently in `volume_zone`, we consider topology label and beta label as different labels. That is ,if we have a pv with `LabelFailureDomainBetaZone` and a node with `LabelTopologyZone`, even if they have same values, `volume_zone` will `not` let the pod pass filter. If we're going to remove beta labels on node,maybe we should try to consider two labels as the same in `volume_zone`?
***
Here's my understanding:
- For migrated volumes, we translate Topology labels to pv.NodeAffinity and update the pv, then we skip volume_zone(that is,don't compare labels with nodes).
- What about non-migratable volumes, I think we should continue to compare pv.labels with node labels for non-migratable volumes?

title: Kubelet creates leases without ownerReference set if node doesn't exist
description:
### What happened?

* Some external controller deleted node object while kubelet was alive
* Due to ignoring errors in kubelet's lease logic, it created lease without ownerReference set

### What did you expect to happen?

* Kubelet doesn't create lease without ownerReference set in any case, even pathological one

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Some external controller deletes node object
* Garbage collector properly deletes associated lease object
* Kubelet tries to update object and it fails on Conflict (saying that UID doesn't match): 
  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b1e130fe83156783153538b6d79821c2fdaa85bb/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L179-L198
* We go to `apierrors.IsConflict(err)` branch, call backoffEnsureLease and assign result to base, but backoffEnsureLease may return potentially invalid object if ensureLease returned error (which happens when newLeasePostProcessFunc returns error, e.g. when node doesn't exist).
* We `continue`
* The next loop calls c.newLease on the incorrect base and ignores error in line 181 (so the second attempt to call newLeasePostProcessFunc which also fails with an error) 
* We do UPDATE with incomplete (without effect of newLeasePostProcessFunc) object
* Given that leases allow CreateOnUpdate a new object, without ownerReference is created: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b1e130fe83156783153538b6d79821c2fdaa85bb/pkg/registry/coordination/lease/strategy.go#L65-L68

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

comments.text: need to understand what is the right behavior here

We are in trouble for this problem too. 

I think It’s exactly as @mborsz said.
Lease has the special update endpoint which can create the new lease objects not only update them.
If it receives a request with a new lease object which has non-nil UID field, **returns a conflict error**.

This situation can be occured in the [retryUpdateLease](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6ed938fc8f3a9d99e5e0347c57055678891739a4/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L177-L198) function when a lease object is deleted.  The lease object is deleted when the node resource is deleted in the result of GC.

When received a conflict error in updating a lease object and the parent node object doesn't exist, [the base variable is set with nil by the ensureLease function](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6ed938fc8f3a9d99e5e0347c57055678891739a4/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L189-L192), and continue next loop. In the next loop, the [newLease](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6ed938fc8f3a9d99e5e0347c57055678891739a4/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/apimachinery/lease/controller.go#L181) function returns the new lease object without ownerReference and UID. As a result, it is created unexpectively by the special update endpoint.

title: Kubelet log query errors "input contains unsupported characters"
description:
### What happened?

I enabled the [kubelet log query feature](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#log-query) on EKS 1.27.4 using Ubuntu 20.04.6.

When I try to query the kubelet logs or log files from the system I get the error "input contains unsupported characters"

```
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/i-0ede67f2d75dfe308.us-west-2.compute.internal/proxy/logs/?query=snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service"
Error from server (NotAcceptable): query: Invalid value: "snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service": input contains unsupported characters

kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/i-0ede67f2d75dfe308.us-west-2.compute.internal/proxy/logs/?query=cloud-init.log"
Error from server (NotAcceptable): query: Invalid value: "cloud-init.log": input contains unsupported characters
```
The systemd kubelet service runs as a snap called `snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service` and I _think_ that might be the source of this problem (running the kubelet in a snap), but I'm not sure if it's intended to work. The fact that I couldn't see /var/log file query was surprising and the error message is misleading which is why I'm opening an issue here.

I followed the same configuration steps on Amazon Linux 2 and it works as expected.

### What did you expect to happen?

Log query should work on Ubuntu or provide a clearer error message.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This should be reproducible on any Kubernetes cluster running Ubuntu with Kubelet in a snap, but this is what I did.

Install [eksdemo](https://github.com/awslabs/eksdemo) to make cluster creation and karpenter setup easier)
```
eksdemo create cluster log-testing --os Ubuntu2004 --prefix-assignment
```
Install Karpenter as a node autoscaler. This will automatically create a provisioner and AWSNodeTemplate objects.
```
eksdemo install autoscaling karpenter -c ubuntu -A Ubuntu
```
Modify the AWSNodeTemplate with userdata that can customize Ubuntu with log query enabled
```
cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: karpenter.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: AWSNodeTemplate
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  amiFamily: Ubuntu
  securityGroupSelector:
    aws:eks:cluster-name: ubuntu
  subnetSelector:
    Name: eksctl-ubuntu-cluster/SubnetPrivate*
  userData: |
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e

    # This probably isn't the best way to do this but it worked
    sed -i 's/args="$KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS"/args="--feature-gates=NodeLogQuery=true $KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS"/g' /etc/eks/bootstrap.sh
    sed -i '/# writes kubeReserved and evictionHard/a echo "$(jq .enableSystemLogHandler=true $KUBELET_CONFIG)" > $KUBELET_CONFIG' /etc/eks/bootstrap.sh
    sed -i '/# writes kubeReserved and evictionHard/a echo "$(jq .enableSystemLogQuery=true $KUBELET_CONFIG)" > $KUBELET_CONFIG' /etc/eks/bootstrap.sh
EOF
```
Deploy a workload that uses hostname spread to get more nodes.
```
cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  minAvailable: "80%"
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: public.ecr.aws/eks-distro/kubernetes/pause:3.2
        name: myapp
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "1"
            memory: 256M
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: host-zone-spread
        maxSkew: 2
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: host-zone-spread
        maxSkew: 5
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
EOF
```
When the new Ubuntu node is created you can log into the node with session manager. I like to use [ssm-helpers](https://github.com/disneystreaming/ssm-helpers)
```
brew install disneystreaming/tap/ssm-helpers
ssm session
# select the new node
```
You can verify that the kubelet is running and logging is enabled
```
sudo systemctl status -l snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service
```
Now you can try to query logs
```
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$NODE/proxy/logs/?query=snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service"
```

### Anything else we need to know?

This works with AL2. You can test with a different AWSNodeTemplate that uses AL2 instead
```
cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: karpenter.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: AWSNodeTemplate

  name: default
spec:
  amiFamily: AL2
  securityGroupSelector:
    aws:eks:cluster-name: ubuntu
  subnetSelector:
    Name: eksctl-ubuntu-cluster/SubnetPrivate*
  userData: |
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e

    cat << EOF > /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/90-kubelet-extra-args.conf
    [Service]
    Environment="KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--feature-gates=NodeLogQuery=true $KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS"
    EOF
    systemctl daemon-reload

    echo "$(jq '.enableSystemLogHandler=true' /etc/kubernetes/kubelet/kubelet-config.json)" > /etc/kubernetes/kubelet/kubelet-config.json
    echo "$(jq '.enableSystemLogQuery=true' /etc/kubernetes/kubelet/kubelet-config.json)" > /etc/kubernetes/kubelet/kubelet-config.json
EOF
```

description:
### What happened?

Why PatchService method is used for deleting finalizers in cloud-controller-manager,
[https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L922 ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L922 )
```golang

func (c *Controller) removeFinalizer(service *v1.Service) error {
	if !servicehelper.HasLBFinalizer(service) {
		return nil
	}
	// Make a copy so we don't mutate the shared informer cache.
	updated := service.DeepCopy()
	updated.ObjectMeta.Finalizers = removeString(updated.ObjectMeta.Finalizers, servicehelper.LoadBalancerCleanupFinalizer)

	klog.V(2).Infof("Removing finalizer from service %s/%s", updated.Namespace, updated.Name)
	_, err := servicehelper.PatchService(c.kubeClient.CoreV1(), service, updated)
	return err
}
``` 
This method updates with service/status,
```golang

func PatchService(c corev1.CoreV1Interface, oldSvc, newSvc *v1.Service) (*v1.Service, error) {
	// Reset spec to make sure only patch for Status or ObjectMeta.
	newSvc.Spec = oldSvc.Spec

	patchBytes, err := getPatchBytes(oldSvc, newSvc)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	return c.Services(oldSvc.Namespace).Patch(context.TODO(), oldSvc.Name, types.StrategicMergePatchType, patchBytes, metav1.PatchOptions{}, "status")

}
```
[https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/service/helpers/helper.go#L132](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/service/helpers/helper.go#L132)

service nodeport be released promptly when service is deleted.

create a loadblancer service with nodeport seted,then delete it and recreate.

The Service "svc-not-tolerate-unready" is invalid: spec.ports[0].nodePort: Invalid value: 30999: provided port is already allocated

```

	// Reset spec to make sure only patch for Status or ObjectMeta.
	newSvc.Spec = oldSvc.Spec

title: Cloud provider implementations do not show provider-specific options in usage string
description:
### What happened?

The `NewCloudControllerManagerCommand` function in `k8s.io/cloud-provider/app/controllermanager.go` accepts an `additionalFlags` parameter which it describes as a way to "controller specific flags to be included in the complete set of controller manager flags". However, when the usage string is shown (either via `$cmd --help` or when parsing options fails), these additional options are not included in the usage string.	

This was identified via code inspection while trying to figure out what options did in `openstack-cloud-controller-manager`.

### What did you expect to happen?

For e.g. `aws-cloud-controller-manager`, the output of `aws-cloud-controller-manager --help` should include a `Tagging Controller Options` section corresponding to [the flagset registered for that command](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws/blob/v1.28.1/cmd/aws-cloud-controller-manager/main.go#L67-L83). This section should in turn list all of [the options added to that flagset](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws/blob/v1.28.1/pkg/controllers/options/tagging_controller.go#L30-L38).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Build a cloud provider executable that includes additional options, such as `aws-cloud-controller-manager`
2. Run `$cmd --help`
3. Observe the additional options are not shown in the output

title: Transient Driver Registration on the CSINode can Result in Missed NodeUnstageVolume RPCs During Pod Migration
description:
### What happened?

In `unmountDetachDevices` (see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go#L279-L316)) we have the following code that will ultimately dispatch `NodeUnstageVolume` RPCs to the underlying CSI plugin.

Here is a pseudo-code representation of the current logic:

```
function unmountDetachDevices
	for all unmounted volumes in ASoW
		if volume not in DSoW &&
		   not operation pending on volume
			if device is mounted globally or
			   device is mounted uncertain
				Case A:
				unmount device
				(this will kick off the NodeUnstageVolume RPC; we want to be here)
			else
				Case B:
				just remove volume from ASoW
				(general badness since we don't issue a NodeUnstageVolume RPC)
```

In our testbeds, we have observed a number of occurrences where we fall into `Case B` when the CSI Node plugin for a particular driver is being bounced, which leads to the volumemanager failing to dispatch the `NodeUnstageVolume` RPC. If the pod migrates to another node, this will leave behind a Zombie LUN in our testbeds (we're using iSCSI).

A Zombie LUN can and often does result in corruption when other pods later migrate to the node in question.

Based on testing that we conducted, we discovered that this case occurs because the device is marked as unmounted.

Initially, we see the device marked as uncertain during reconstruction.

However, if the CSI Node driver pod is bounced in the exact window when a `NodeStageVolume` RPC is issued, then we end up [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L777C1-L798C2).

There we check to see if the error encountered is a “transient error” or a “final error”; if a “final error” is encountered, then the device state transitions from uncertain to unmounted. That is what is happening in our case.

The error is generated when the CSIClient cannot find the requested driver [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/volume/csi/csi_client.go#L158C1-L161C3).

The driver registration code is socket based; based on our testing, if the Node plugin goes down for any reason the driver registration is removed from the CSINode.

Now for the `NodePublishVolume` path, this is mitigated by wrapping the error in a transient error [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/volume/csi/csi_mounter.go#L109C3-L109C3) (I assume to avoid such state transitions?):

```
	csi, err := c.csiClientGetter.Get()
	if err != nil {
		return volumetypes.NewTransientOperationFailure(log("mounter.SetUpAt failed to get CSI client: %v", err))
	}
```

Based on our testing to date, adding parity [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go#L290) to the `NodeStageVolume` path would help us avoid Zombie LUNs in our test setups due to missing `NodeUnstageVolume` calls:

```
	// lets check if node/unstage is supported
	if c.csiClient == nil {
		c.csiClient, err = newCsiDriverClient(csiDriverName(csiSource.Driver))
		if err != nil {
			return errors.New(log("attacher.MountDevice failed to create newCsiDriverClient: %v", err))
		}
	}
	csi := c.csiClient
```

This can be fixed by also wrapping this error in a transient error.

### What did you expect to happen?

We expected to see a `NodeUnstageVolume` call coming to the underlying NodePlugin (once it was finally back up).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Force reconstruction on a node.
* Take down the CSI node plugin on the node while pods are mounting.
* Try to migrate the pod to another node; the underlying machinery will correctly wait for the plugin to come back up before proceeding.
* Later, bring up the CSI node plugin.
* While the pod migration might be successful, a `NodeUnstageVolume` should be missing if the correct timing windows were hit.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: App container is started before initContainers could complete on node reboot
description:
### What happened?

On node reboot, we see app container is started before initContainers could complete. Essentially both app and initContainers are running in parallel. We are using initContainers to ensure dependent drivers are loaded by other pod before the app container could start. But because app container is starting in parallel, they hit a failure. This was not seen with k8s 1.27 and only happening with 1.28. Also, this happens only on node reboot, not during fresh install of our application (gpu-operator)

confirmed that this is NOT reproduced in 1.27. It is a regression.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3cf3702d1e638548ba9fcfd957ebae43e1a573cb/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container.go#L886-L890

This happens because the kubelet uses the old container statuses to check if the pod has been initialized before.

Before 1.28, the kubelet considers the pod as initialized if there is any regular container running.
However, with 1.28, the kubelet considers the pod as initialized if there is any regular container running OR EXITED.

I think the latter one is theoretically right, but currently, we cannot know if the container statuses are from the current pod sandbox or the old one.

The fix would be,
1. check if the container statuses are outdated (not sure how to do this yet...)
2. (workaround) revert pod initialization check: there is any regular container running or exited => there is any regular container running

The refactored / new methods could be kept in a different file and only called when the feature gate was enabled. That would restore 1.28 to match 1.27 behavior by default as quickly as possible.

title: The nodeIP passed to kube proxiers is invalid
description:
### What happened?

With primary ipFamily="IPv4" in v1.27.4:
```
I0723 11:44:55.051869     359 proxier.go:405] "Record nodeIP and family" nodeIP="0.0.0.0" family=IPv4
I0723 11:44:55.052182     359 proxier.go:405] "Record nodeIP and family" nodeIP="::" family=IPv6
```
On "master":
```
I0723 11:46:29.622648     357 proxier.go:405] "Record nodeIP and family" nodeIP="192.168.1.2" family="IPv4"
I0723 11:46:29.622730     357 proxier.go:405] "Record nodeIP and family" nodeIP="::" family="IPv6"
```
So some correction has been made, but IPv6 is still incorrect, even though an IPv6 address is configured for the node:
```
# kubectl get node vm-002 -o json | jq .status.addresses
[
  {
    "address": "192.168.1.2",
    "type": "InternalIP"
  },
  {
    "address": "fd00::c0a8:102",
    "type": "InternalIP"
  },
  {
    "address": "vm-002",
    "type": "Hostname"
  }
]
```

With primary ipFamily="IPv6", the kube-proxy `bindAddress` seem to be used:
```
I0723 11:40:33.843305     366 proxier.go:405] "Record nodeIP and family" nodeIP="0.0.0.0" family="IPv4"
I0723 11:40:33.843392     366 proxier.go:405] "Record nodeIP and family" nodeIP="::1" family="IPv6"
```



### What did you expect to happen?

The nodeIP address for the correct family as configured in the node object should be passed as `nodeIP` to kube-proxiers

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Start `kube-proxy` with log-level >=2 and grep the logs for:
```
"Record nodeIP and family"
```

### Anything else we need to know?

The `nodeIP` seem to be used in just one place in both proxiers:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d0814fa476c72201dcc599297171fe65fb657908/pkg/proxy/ipvs/proxier.go#L1227-L1230

`allowFromNode` will be false for an unspecified (any) address regardless of the *real* nodeIP..

I wanted to use `nodeIP` as "src" for routes, that's how I discovered this problem, but in any case, nodeIP should be correct

### Kubernetes version

v1.27.4 and master

### Cloud provider

N/A

### OS version

comments.text:
To use the `bindAddress` was intentional, but for dual-stack that only gives one address.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d0814fa476c72201dcc599297171fe65fb657908/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L915-L919

### Proxy-mode=iptables

Proxier.nodeIP is only used to determine `allowFromNode`

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97c7dbcd227ec253bb277a91575706fe30f519dc/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1306-L1328

`cidr.Contains()` return "false" for an unspecified address, so for the "secondary" family the additional rule is never added. If the nodeIP is localhost, it *should* never cause allowFromNode=true since it's pointless to add localhost (127.0.0.0/8) in `loadBalancerSourceRanges` (a packet localhost->loadBalancerIP would be a "martian").

So the *only* case when the additional rule is added (allowFromNode=true) is when a loadBalancerSourceRange contains a "real" nodeIP. To allow the bindAddress to possibly override the nodeIP may feel tempting, but the bindAddress is usually configured in the config-file (or configMap), so it's very hard for normal K8s users to set it "per-node".

The additional rule in only needed if the loadBalancerIP is also assigned to a local interface on the node. I think that's rare for proxy-mode=iptables, so I think that's why nobody have encountered this bug.

### Proxy-mode=ipvs

The loadBalancerIP's are **always** added to `kube-ipvs0` so the `allowFromNode` thing as in proxy-mode=iptables isn't feasible. It may be removed.

On the other hand, for proxy-mode=ipvs you can't restrict access to the loadBalancerIP from the node with `loadBalancerSourceRanges`!

So a better alternative may be to use it "the other way around": block access unless allowFromNode=true. But that should be another issue (and PR)

title: Conntrack cleaning happens before network programming endpoints
description:
### What happened?

Currently kube-proxy efficiently cleans all stale conntrack entries preventing traffic black holing for deleted endpoints, but there can be some corner cases when conntrack cleaning happens before programming the network leaving a small window in which if any packet arrives will back-hole the traffic.

The corner case:
Taking a simple case of load-balancer service backed by a deployment with single replica, on deleting the pod(gracefully), I observed two **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocations:
1.  First one with EndpointConditions.Ready as false
2. EndpointSlice was cleared for the pod 

The conntrack flow for this case:
1. After processing the first **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocation **EndpointsMap** will still have entries for the pod as endpoint still exists, though not in ready state so proxier won't program deletion of endpoint from the data path. But the endpoint IP will be picked for conntrack cleaning as new endpoint != old endpoint because of the not ready condition.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95e915c4288eda15da1724989f3f7dec9f3512d6/pkg/proxy/endpoints.go#L423-L436
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95e915c4288eda15da1724989f3f7dec9f3512d6/pkg/proxy/endpoints.go#L120-L126

2.  After processing the second **OnEndpointSliceUpdate** invocation **EndpointsMap** won't have entries for the endpoint and the proxier will program deletion of the endpoint in the data path. EndpointIP won't be picked up for conntrack cleaning as the following logic will skip it
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/95e915c4288eda15da1724989f3f7dec9f3512d6/pkg/proxy/endpoints.go#L417-L421

This behaviour leads to conntrack cleaning one cycle ahead of network programming.  
This might be a regression of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/106163

### What did you expect to happen?

Conntrack cleanup should happen after programming the network.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This behaviour can be observed in kube-proxy logs (verbosity=4).
[link to log snippet showing the behaviour](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119010#issuecomment-1622325495)

I used the following objects for experimenting:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: test
  labels:
    app: test
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: test
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        kubernetes.io/hostname: kind-worker2
      containers:
      - name: test
        image: registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.45
        command:
          - /agnhost
        args:
          - netexec
          - --udp-port=80
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: test
  ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      name: udp
      nodePort: 31111
      port: 80
      targetPort: 80
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: Kubernetes api returns incorrect conflicting fields during server-side apply in some cases
description:
### What happened?

When performing a server-side apply PATCH request, if there are conflicts in what's being applied with differing field owners, kubernetes responds with a 409 conflict error with an array of causes in the error detail, enumerating the conflicting fields that were discovered.

In some cases, we see that the fields returned in this 409 error response are incorrect, containing both duplicate fields, and entirely missing other conflicts.

### What did you expect to happen?

The http 409 error response when receiving a conflict while using server-side apply should contain all of the correct fields (and also ideally no duplicates).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Save this file as `original.yaml`

<details>

```yaml
kind: DaemonSet
apiVersion: apps/v1
metadata:
  name: simple-probe
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      k8s-app: simple-probe
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        k8s-app: simple-probe
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: probe
        image: registry.k8s.io/busybox
        args:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - touch /tmp/healthy; sleep 9999999
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - cat
            - /tmp/healthy
          periodSeconds: 5
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - cat
            - /tmp/healthy
          periodSeconds: 5
```

</details>

Save this file as `modified.yaml`

<details>

```yaml
kind: DaemonSet
apiVersion: apps/v1
metadata:
  name: simple-probe
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: probe
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - ls
            - /tmp/healthy
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - ls
            - /tmp/healthy
          periodSeconds: 10
```

</details>

Now apply the first yaml with server-side apply:

`kubectl apply -f original.yaml --server-side --field-manager=original`

Apply the second yaml with server-side apply, using a different field manager:

`kubectl apply -f modified.yaml --server-side --field-manager=modified --validate=false --force-conflicts`

If we get the applied daemonset at this point (`kubectl get ds simple-probe -o yaml --show-managed-fields`), everything appears to be applied correctly with expected behavior and expected field owners

Now try to re-apply with the original command/field manager, forcing a conflict error to be returned (increased verbosity to see returned http body):

`kubectl apply -f original.yaml --server-side --field-manager=original -v=9`

When re-applying this original yaml (without force-conflicts), we expect to observe conflicts on all of the fields that were changed by modified.yaml and now owned by the `modified` field manager. These _should_ be:
```
.spec.template.spec.containers[name="probe"].livenessProbe.exec.command
.spec.template.spec.containers[name="probe"].livenessProbe.periodSeconds
.spec.template.spec.containers[name="probe"].readinessProbe.exec.command
.spec.template.spec.containers[name="probe"].readinessProbe.periodSeconds
```

However, this is the response we get when trying to apply using the increased verbosity command:

```
I0706 12:56:34.394111   74086 request.go:1188] Request Body: {"apiVersion":"apps/v1","kind":"DaemonSet","metadata":{"name":"simple-probe","namespace":"default"},"spec":{"selector":{"matchLabels":{"k8s-app":"simple-probe"}},"template":{"metadata":{"labels":{"k8s-app":"simple-probe"}},"spec":{"containers":[{"args":["/bin/sh","-c","touch /tmp/healthy; sleep 9999999"],"image":"registry.k8s.io/busybox","livenessProbe":{"exec":{"command":["cat","/tmp/healthy"]},"periodSeconds":5},"name":"probe","readinessProbe":{"exec":{"command":["cat","/tmp/healthy"]},"periodSeconds":5}}]}}}}
I0706 12:56:34.394215   74086 round_trippers.go:466] curl -v -XPATCH  -H "Accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/apply-patch+yaml" -H "User-Agent: kubectl/v1.27.3 (darwin/amd64) kubernetes/25b4e43" 'https://<REDACTED>/apis/apps/v1/namespaces/default/daemonsets/simple-probe?fieldManager=original&fieldValidation=Strict&force=false'
I0706 12:56:34.408095   74086 round_trippers.go:553] PATCH https://<REDACTED>/apis/apps/v1/namespaces/default/daemonsets/simple-probe?fieldManager=original&fieldValidation=Strict&force=false 409 Conflict in 13 milliseconds
I0706 12:56:34.408123   74086 round_trippers.go:570] HTTP Statistics: GetConnection 0 ms ServerProcessing 13 ms Duration 13 ms
I0706 12:56:34.408133   74086 round_trippers.go:577] Response Headers:
I0706 12:56:34.408142   74086 round_trippers.go:580]     Date: Thu, 06 Jul 2023 19:56:34 GMT

error: Apply failed with 4 conflicts: conflicts with "modified":

```

Note that the conflicts returned by the 409 error have duplicate fields, and completely omit at least 3 of the fields we are actually conflicting with.

### Anything else we need to know?

If we re-apply the original with `--force-conflicts`, then the correct data is applied, and the correct field managers are set, however if we do not want to force conflicts, the conflicting fields returned in the 409 error returned from the API server are incorrect.

title: DaemonSet fails to scale down during the rolling update when `maxUnavailable=0`
description:
### What happened?

I have a daemonset with the rolling update strategy. I have `maxSurge` parameter set to a non zero value [which means](https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes/blob/cb4b47e5ddfbaf7844237b2e2eb2b0acfed5f1b5/pkg/apis/apps/validation/validation.go#L394-L402) that the `maxUnavailable` parameter is set to `0`. When I replace the toleration in the daemonset's template spec from the one which helped me to be scheduled on the master node into any other toleration, I see the new pods still trying to be scheduled on the master nodes. The old pods from the tolerated nodes can be lucky enough to be recreated but only if they go before any pod from the intolerable node.

title: "Connection reset by peer" due to invalid conntrack packets
description:
### What happened?

When packets with sequence number out-of-window arrived k8s node, conntrack marked them as INVALID. kube-proxy will ignore them, without rewriting DNAT. However, there is no corresponding session link on the host, and the host sends a reset packet, causing the session link to be interrupted

### What did you expect to happen?

connection not reset

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/74839

### Anything else we need to know?

This problem can be solved by command：
iptables -t filter -I INPUT -p tcp -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP

Similar issue:https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/74839
But this issue "drop" is placed on the forward chain, our scenario needs to be placed on the input chain.

IMO kube-proxy should not set any sysctls that are not literally _required_ for functionality that the user has explicitly opted into (eg `net.ipv4.ip_forward` for most network plugins). Kube-proxy does not own the host network namespace, and it should not be doing things that will affect _other people's_ host-network traffic, because if we do it's going to break some users. (See also: #94861.)

We can document that we think it's a good idea for users/distros to set `ip_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal`, and if we think it's almost always a better idea than not, we can warn at startup if it's not set, but (IMO) we shouldn't set it ourselves.

If we can get the same effect with an iptables rule that only affects kube-proxy's own traffic, then I think that's better than setting a sysctl that will also affect non-kube-proxy traffic.

That says "this problem will occur if conntrack is unable to recognize a packet", but it doesn't explain the *real-world scenario* that causes conntrack to be unable to recognize a packet.

If we go to the kernel developers and say "manually injecting random incorrect packets into a conntrack'ed connection causes it to get confused", then they'll likely respond either "don't do that then" or "use `nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal`".

There are three potential "fixes" here:
1. If this is unambiguously a conntrack bug, then we should figure out the details, and get the kernel devs to fix it. However, getting kernel bug fixes into all k8s clusters in the world takes "a long time", so even if it is a kernel bug, we should still think about the other fixes.
2. Individual cluster admins can use `nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal`. We should advertise this better, but we feel that it would be dubious to have kube-proxy set this flag itself (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117924#issuecomment-1548163880).
3. As per https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94861#issuecomment-1626025213 we could probably tweak the existing rule so that it didn't interfere with non-k8s packets ~and as suggested by the OP of this issue, we could add a similar rule to the INPUT chain (though this would need a bit of further thinking about to make sure we weren't introducing any new conflicts with non-k8s traffic)~.

We _could_ revert the DROP rules and tell people to use the sysctl instead (and actually, probably that's a better answer for _this_ issue than adding a new DROP rule to the INPUT chain is). But we'd need to warn users in advance if we were going to do that, since it would break existing clusters.

> Also, If we revert the DROP rule, which can solve the routing asymmetry issue mentioned in #94861, which is a big fix for us😄

but the change to only apply the DROP rule to pod traffic should also fix that

> Do we need a flag to decide if we need the DROP rule?

In our case, the pods of the external cluster subnet failed to access the pods of the cluster subnet to connect due to asymmetric routing, So the packet still matches The DROP rule to pod.
 
> In the latter case, we might want to make the transition via a feature gate

Do we need a KEP for this or only a feature gate?

In general, feature gates imply KEPs (and any change that will take multiple releases to complete, where we want to make sure we don't forget about it halfway through, should get a KEP, because we have processes for tracking those).

It doesn't have to be a _big_ KEP, and some of the sections of the KEP template will be irrelevant and can be omitted, because you're not introducing a new feature. (See https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4005 for example.)

> In the latter case, we might want to make the transition via a feature gate. Then people who need asymmetric routing to work can enable the feature gate in Alpha (to make kube-proxy stop creating the DROP rule), and people who need high-traffic services to work but who didn't get the memo about using the sysctl can _disable_ the feature gate in Beta until they have a chance to update their node configs to set the right sysctl.

If we skip a KEP, make sure that the release team know to track the details (comms, docs, etc) as if it were a KEP. This is an important thing to track.
Should we at least triage this as Accepted?

Some alternatives

1. remove DROP rule and ask users to set sysctl `ip_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal` (I'm not in favor per my previous comment and the least surprise principle)
2. remove DROP rule and we set sysctl `ip_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal` 
3. only set DROP rule if `ip_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal` is not set
4. control the DROP rule with a flag/config so users can opt-out if don't want to set it (they can decide to use the sysctl or live with that risk)
5. ...

I can accept KEP, but I think this may take multiple releases to complete. how about this?

- We remove the DROP rule
- Control the sysctl with a flag or a feature-gate.

If it's a flag, I believe it's relatively simple and we can finish it in 1.29. In the case of feature-gate, this may take multiple releases to complete.
If [REDACTED] sets the `nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal` to true by default, we can safely remove the DROP rule

title: kube-proxy: Drop packets in INVALID state drops packets from outside the pod range
description:
**What happened**:
When kube-proxy is configured with a cluster-cidr range, it drops packets with an INVALID conntrack state for all sources on the KUBE-FORWARD chain. This is meant to prevent spurious retransmits in long-lived TCP connections to a service IP, but it prevents clusters from having asymmetrical routing on private subnets with services outside of a cluster. 

**What you expected to happen**:
Packets on the KUBE-FORWARD chain with an INVALID conntrack state should be dropped for only sources inside of the cluster-cidr if set.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
N/A

**Anything else we need to know?**:
Change to drop INVALID conntrack packets was in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/74840. Backing out that commit and compiling is my current workaround.

See [the blog post I linked earlier](https://www.growse.com/2020/01/23/adventures-with-asymmetric-routing-and-firewalls.html) for an example of a similar setup.

> mark only out of window RST segments as INVALID

are the packets on your asymmetric routing setup marked as invalid if you set `nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal=1`? it should only mark the ones that are out of window per the description
I'd love to pin this down, but I don't have the means to set up a repro.  Is there a way I can set up a way to experiment?

We were bit by this too after revisiting an old service that had been unused since the heady days of pre-#74840, and would also like to see the proposed patch merged (or a configuration option to prevent insertion of the INVALID state drop rule - either suits us).

I unfortunately don't have any useful input as to setting up for reproduction. In our case we have a pretty odd anycast set up with a small pool of (public) addresses managed by calico. 

However I do seem to have a dirty workaround for small clusters. By setting notrack (ctstate UNTRACKED?) in the raw table for packets in our specific ranges that would otherwise match ctstate INVALID, the packets aren't dropped. Which may be of help to someone else who finds this issue.

We are seeing something very similar on large file downloads and our issue exactly fits this one's subject.
These RESET (corrected after @aojea) are happening intermittently and I am seeing similar behavior mentioned in the blog mentioned below. I am unsure if someone has found a workaround for this issue or not, so yeah my +1 to this issue being looked up by the community.

> @aojea I don't understand how that will help me here. The packets with a ctstate INVALID are not generated due to conntrack saturation ([as described here](https://technology.lastminute.com/chasing-k8s-connection-reset-issue/)), but due to asymmetric routing in our network. See [the blog post I linked earlier](https://www.growse.com/2020/01/23/adventures-with-asymmetric-routing-and-firewalls.html) for an example of a similar setup.
@abhiTamrakar We're using https://github.com/kakao/network-node-manager as a solution for the connection reset we were seeing and might fix this issue.

Let me try to avoid that this thread derails and see if I can get current status:

> These REJECTs are happening intermittently and I am seeing similar behavior mentioned in the blog mentioned below.

1. kube-proxy install rules to drop INVALID cstate connections, this solves the ~REJECT~ RESET problems
2. there are some scenarios, with asymmetric routing per example, that this rules may drop unrelated traffic.

The request is to remove the rule that drops those INVALID states or to try to restrict it, and that can cause that people start to have the  ~REJECT~ RESET problems and drops again.

If we have a reproducer we can be more precise in the final solution, but removing one rule without any strong evidence in kube-proxy is very risky

As a workaround for the asymetric routing problem, I suggested to set the nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal on the kernel:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal=1
```
I think that will solve the problems, it will be good if someone can test it and provide feedback

No sadly, its my bad, it is not REJECT, it is RESET that's happening and conntrack has nothing to do with it, mostly (I hope). Kubeproxy is doing what is intended but specifically when there are external agents in play, the packet doesn't sends an ACK back to the response of SYN-ACK.
Our case, we hit A to initiate a download, A calls B to get the action completed to generate download data for the user finally via their browser.
A and B both are on k8s, we saw A starts and a complete cycle goes for sometime until there multiple parallel downloads requested where few gets completed and few gets a RESET.
On primary debugging, it appears that RESET was getting invoked by the pod but pod is just sending a RST-ACK not RST itself.
The missing packet is never found in the default route, unless we see that there is a chance where ACK is missed and we found some lines in tcpdump with missing sequence for ACKs. Thats why i doubt my issue is related here.

One more weird coincidence is few downloads have spurious transmission.

> @abhiTamrakar We're using https://github.com/kakao/network-node-manager as a solution for the connection reset we were seeing and might fix this issue.

Thankyou, I will take a look, but mostly I would like to wait before using it, debug more to understand the actual cause and then act on it.

sorry , I wanted to say RESET, thanks for catching it.
If you think is different and you can provide information and how to reproduce it, I suggest you to open a new issue

I will sure do, when it is different. For now I would like to watch and submit my findings if it is related.
PS: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal=1 is already implemented and we are testing if it does something helpful. so far it doesn't looks like it. thanks for your help.
