title: Unexpected Pod creation delay after recreating Jobs with same names
description:
### What happened?

Pod creations are delayed for up to 10 minutes after creating a Job, which is previously deleted as well as its pods in foreground deletion.

I noticed this case while using [jobset](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/jobset), which when notices a pod failure, it deletes all Jobs and Pods (controlled by jobset spec) then creates new Jobs with same names. After creation of new jobs, I found some Jobs had no Pods. I observed the following logs:

```
"enqueueing job" logger="job-controller" key="default/base-100-workers-0" delay="0"
"enqueueing job" logger="job-controller" key="default/base-100-workers-0" delay="9m35.78848664s"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

Since jobs are newly created, there should no delays in creating their pods.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. setup a k8s cluster with a few nodes
2. install jobset
3. apply below jobset

```
apiVersion: jobset.x-k8s.io/v1alpha2
kind: JobSet
metadata:
  annotations:
    alpha.jobset.sigs.k8s.io/exclusive-topology: cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool
  name: base-100
  namespace: default
spec:
  failurePolicy:
    maxRestarts: 2000
    restartStrategy: Recreate
  network:
    enableDNSHostnames: true
    publishNotReadyAddresses: true
  replicatedJobs:
  - name: workers
    replicas: 4
    template:
      metadata: {}
      spec:
        backoffLimit: 0
        completionMode: Indexed
        completions: 30
        parallelism: 30
        template:
          metadata: {}
          spec:
            containers:
            - name: pi
              image: busybox
              command: ["sh",  "-c", "sleep 10 && exit 10"]
              resources: {}
            restartPolicy: Never
            terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0
```

You should see the delays in pod creation or similar logs from job controller.

### Anything else we need to know?

Those setup creates a JobSet and since the Pods fails after running for a few seconds, the JobSet controller deletes all 4 Jobs and Pods, then create 4 new Jobs with the same names. For example, base-100-workers-[0|1|2|3] and keys used in the [queue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L592) and [podBackoffStore](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L912) are identical if job names are the same.

The bug is likely caused by the race condition:

* t0: job0 (v0) is created
* t1: pods of job0 are created and running
* t2: pods fail and job controller records a backoff record with key default/job0 due the to non-zero number of failed Pods
* t3: job0 and pods are deleted by Jobset controller, deletion events are not yet processed by job controller
* t4: job0 (v1) is created
* t5: job0 creation event is processed by job controller and syncJob() [gets the backoffRecord](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L912) with key default/job0, which is old record from previous job
* t6: job controller gets non-zero remainingTime in [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1709) so it enqueues the job0 task again to delay the pod creation

It appears to me that we need to use a better key in backoffRecordStore to fix this bug or strictly guarantee the sequence of processing Job/Pod events, which will delete the old records from backoffRecordStore.

comments.text:
Could you see if you can reproduce without JobSet?

Ideally it would be great to cover this with a e2e test if we fix this.

Thank you for reporting 👍 

I suspect this is because the `key` used for backoffStore (tracking the backoff delay) is the Job name/namespace (see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b65f712d2cb70a358e9c77d02b21874c14d3d1ba/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L912)). 

I believe the simplest fix is to replace the key as UID. 

Alternatively use string or struct embedding name, namespace and UID. Similarly as we did for [`orphanPodKey`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b65f712d2cb70a358e9c77d02b21874c14d3d1ba/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L159C6-L165). However, it is a complication, and we don't log the keys currently anyway when accessing backoff_utils.

I'm leaning slightly to simplicity -  going with just UID. 

As for the fix PR it would be great to have a reproducible scenario in an integration test, I admit it might be tricky. Maybe we can try manipulating the backoff delays as we do in some tests could make it reproducible  [example](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b65f712d2cb70a358e9c77d02b21874c14d3d1ba/test/integration/job/job_test.go#L963).

cc @atiratree

Make sense to have an integration test for it but I am not knowledgeable the integration codebase enough to make a quick change for that. However, the fix PR is relatively easier. It'd be great if we can split it into two tasks.

It seems that this is caused due to the `tp` object being allocated once when the `ResolverEnvOption` is called and then being written to on every call of the `envOption` function later on.

I added a mutex to the `ResolverTypeProvider` struct and locked the write and this seems to fix the issue completely (ran it about 20-30 times), but I'm not familiar enough with the code to understand if this is a good solution/if anything else needs to be guarded in this codepath. 

Here's the change:
```go

func NewResolverTypeProviderAndEnvOption(resolver TypeResolver) (*ResolverTypeProvider, cel.EnvOption) {
	tp := &ResolverTypeProvider{typeResolver: resolver}
	var envOption cel.EnvOption = func(e *cel.Env) (*cel.Env, error) {
		tp.mu.Lock()
		defer tp.mu.Unlock()
		tp.underlyingTypeProvider = e.CELTypeProvider()
		typeProviderOption := cel.CustomTypeProvider(tp)
		return typeProviderOption(e)
	}
	return tp, envOption
}
```

title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler reporting FailedRescale error
description:
### What happened?

We are currently running several applications that are configured with metric-based scaling. These applications are expected to scale frequently in response to varying traffic patterns.

Occasionally, we observe the following error during scaling events (though it is not frequent), and there is no noticeable impact on the actual scaling process:

```
reason: FailedRescale, New size: <size>; reason: All metrics <below>/<above> target; error: Operation cannot be fulfilled on deployments.apps: the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again.
```

Our understanding is that this occurs due to a race condition where another controller or a CI/CD process is simultaneously patching or updating the Deployment object at the same time the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) attempts to scale it.

**In some cases, we observed the issue occurring even when there were no apparent changes to the Deployment object itself. Only a possible update to the resourceVersion, which we were unable to confirm the reason for the same**

To be cautious, we have set up an alert to notify us if the HPA fails to scale a deployment for any reason. However, encountering this specific error results in unnecessary noise and false positives in our alerting system.

### What did you expect to happen?

We expect the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) to perform retries internally and suppress the reporting of this error, as its occurrence generates unnecessary noise and may cause undue concern regarding system scaling.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

To reproduce the issue:

- Configure a Deployment and Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) with CPU or memory-based scaling.
- Apply load to the Deployment pods to trigger scaling by the HPA.
- Simultaneously, perform multiple consecutive patch operations on the Deployment.

This sequence will result in the HPA reporting the same error in its events.

### Anything else we need to know?

NA

title: Kubelet Swap metrics are missing
description:
### What happened?

Kubelet's swap related metrics were introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118865. However, these swap-related metrics are missing from `/metrics/resource` endpoint. Only node-level swap usage metrics are visible. The pod-level and container-level swap usage are available from `/stats/summary` endpoint, but no metrics are visible from `/metrics/resource`.

```
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/metrics/resource" | grep -i swap

### What did you expect to happen?

Container-level swap usage `container_swap_usage_bytes` and pod-level swap usage `pod_swap_usage_bytes` metrics should be available from `/metrics/resource` endpoint.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a node with swap enabled (https://kubernetes.io/blog/2025/03/25/swap-linux-improvements/#install-a-swap-enabled-cluster-with-kubeadm)

Get the swap metrics `kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/<node-name>/proxy/metrics/resource"

The node is using ~~cadvisor~~ CRI for resource metrics.

title: Required field is not actually required
description:
### What happened?

I am trying to solve the mystery of the "required" podSelector field in NetworkPolicy spec. It says that the field is "not optional" https://github.com/kubernetes/api/blob/c3130ba7ba2323372534032dd3153bf331fc59e2/networking/v1/types.go#L66-L68 but at the same time you can create a netpol without podSelector even being set, and it will be populated to the empty selector.
https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#optional-vs-required says
> The API server should not allow POSTing or PUTing a resource with this (required) field unset.

The fun part is that multi-netpol has coped fields from the netpol https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multi-networkpolicy/blob/master/pkg/apis/k8s.cni.cncf.io/v1beta2/types.go#L65C2-L65C55
and (because it is a crd?) it doesn't allow this filed to be unset and returns "The MultiNetworkPolicy is invalid: spec.podSelector: Required value"

### What did you expect to happen?

NetworkPolicy with empty podSelector to be rejected.
CRD and core APIs behave the same way.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

comments.text:
> // An empty podSelector matches all pods in this namespace.

@npinaeva is not that it does not differentiate between "empty" and "unset"?
In the go struct I think so, but it should validate the field is present when I am applying the object, afaik that is how required fields work

For non-pointer, native types would default it to its zero value which is "empty".
For the CRD, the "podSelector" is set to be "required" explicitly for [v1beta1](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multi-networkpolicy/blob/a6d2c547f9f9dc756d285e7015fc32f7b6793f76/scheme.yml#L468-L469) and [v1beta2](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multi-networkpolicy/blob/a6d2c547f9f9dc756d285e7015fc32f7b6793f76/scheme.yml#L924-L925)

I think this is just ambiguity in the way we handle "optional-ness" for built-in types.  There's really no such thing as a non-pointer struct field which is "not set".  It's always there, even if you didn't say anything.  It's not the way I would do it if we started over, believe me.

So the comment says "This field is NOT optional" becuase it's not - it is always present.  But it's not really required, either because an empty selector is semantically meaningful.  After decoding we CAN'T TELL if the user said nothing and got the zero-value or explicitly specified and empty selector.

I think the right thing to do is to change the docs - it IS optional, from the client's point of view, and that's really the way our API docs are written.

The way this is validated is:

```
    allErrs = append(allErrs, unversionedvalidation.ValidateLabelSelector(                                                                             
        &spec.PodSelector,    
        labelSelectorValidationOpts,    
        fldPath.Child("podSelector"),    
    )...)    
```

which turns into:

```
  func ValidateLabelSelector(ps *metav1.LabelSelector, opts LabelSelectorValidationOptions, fldPath *field.Path) field.ErrorList {                     
      allErrs := field.ErrorList{}      
      if ps == nil {                     
          return allErrs  
      }  
      allErrs = append(allErrs, ValidateLabels(ps.MatchLabels, fldPath.Child("matchLabels"))...)  
      for i, expr := range ps.MatchExpressions {  
          allErrs = append(allErrs, ValidateLabelSelectorRequirement(expr, opts, fldPath.Child("matchExpressions").Index(i))...)  
      }                                         
      return allErrs                                           
  }                            
```

So, an empty selector IS considered valid.

I'd like to work on this issue. 
I plan to change the documentation rather than the spec or implementation.
thank you for the clarification! It looks like it is an optional field with the default (zero) value. We can reproduce this behaviour in CRD.

we could add an `+optional` annotation which would stop marking it as required in openapi only (without changing the type or omitempty serialization behavior or validation), since clients can actually submit creation requests that do not include this field

title: Apiserver admission control (validating, mutating webhooks) return misleading response code 400 on network errors
description:
### What happened?

When the apiserver calls a webhook, be it validating or mutating, and the configured endpoint is not reachable due to network issue (timeout, EOF due to a broken connection, rejected new connection, ...) the error defaults to a `400 Bad Request`:

* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go#L309
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/mutating/dispatcher.go#L308

I noticed this when analyzing some random webhook invocation errors and seeing that that the increasing `apiserver_admission_webhook_rejection_count` metric (https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/) had `rejection_code="400"`. This metric was introduced by @roycaihw in PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/81399 to expose the various causes for rejects.

With 4xx being "user side errors" and 5xx being server side errors, this mapping is clearly misleading or even incorrect and I suspected the actual webhook endpoint had responded with a 400.

But the client is clearly NOT at fault here. The 4xx even would indicate that a retry is likely not successful.

### What did you expect to happen?

Non HTTP errors from a failed connection to the webhook endpoint should be mapped to `503 Service Unavailable` with either https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/e25aab096bf1a9b677c0e04efd3870b396494782/pkg/api/errors/errors.go#L339 or even https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/e25aab096bf1a9b677c0e04efd3870b396494782/pkg/api/errors/errors.go#L386 clearly indicating that this is an internal error.

Looking at the handling of response parsing errors in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go#L317-L317 there actually are cased handled with `503`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Register an invalid webhook URL
2. Invoke e.g. a Pod creation and look at the mentioned metrics.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

1.31

comments.text: I just found issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/127335 which seems to be one cause for some of the randomly failing webhook invocations we see. Not that this issue here is not valid, there can always be network issues or crashes of processes.

without looking into much detail into all this issue, I can see these are POST requests

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go#L283

and retrying POST request is usually unsafe, since you don't know if some write operation succeeded

> without looking into much detail into all this issue, I can see these are POST requests
> 
> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9d2fc46556af162ff42a4773349d0f92f9ef8d50/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go#L283
> 
> and retrying POST request is usually unsafe, since you don't know if some write operation succeeded

The retrying (or the fact that 4xx indicates to the client that it or its data is at fault) was just an example of how the wrong status code could be interpreted. 

On a server error (5xx), which I am saying should be used here, it's usually safe for the client to try again.
Even more so, knowing we are talking about stateless webook invocations.

Thinking more about this, returning ANY valid HTTP status code is likely not the proper way if there was no HTTP communication (connection refused, EOF, ...). Certainly the HTTP call from the client (kubectl) maps the failure to reach the webhook to 500 anyway, but looking at e.g. the metrics or logs ... there should be a proper error handling mentioning that there was a connection issue, not some random HTTP code mapping.

There is a similar issue regarding etcd errors https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/112152

@aaron-prindle just accepted that one from triage.
@kubernetes/sig-api-machinery-misc

I agree this should be 5xx.

EDIT: But switching to where we categorize errors too many failures as 500 (when some of them should have been 4xx) would also be wrong
Opened [REDACTED] - please take a look.

title: Incorrect m Suffix in Memory Values for kubectl get hpa
description:
### What happened?

kubectl get hpa incorrectly appends m (millicores) to memory usage values. Memory should always be displayed in bytes, MiB, or GiB, never in "millibytes (m)". This issue also exists in the autoscaling/v2 API, suggesting a deeper problem beyond kubectl

 Affected Versions
Kubernetes Version: v1.29+
kubectl Version: v1.29+
Metrics Server: latest stable
Environment: Affects both on-prem and cloud-managed Kubernetes (e.g., AKS, EKS, GKE).

Deploy an HPA that scales based on memory usage:

yaml

apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: test-hpa
  namespace: default
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: test-deployment
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: memory
        target:
          type: AverageValue
          averageValue: 325Mi
Apply the configuration:

sh

kubectl apply -f test-hpa.yaml
Check HPA details:

sh

kubectl get hpa test-hpa -n default
Observed Output:

bash

NAME      REFERENCE        TARGETS      MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
test-hpa  Deployment/test  171502796800m/325Mi   1         10        2          10m
Problem: The value 171502796800m should not have m, as memory is measured in bytes.

kubectl get --raw "/apis/autoscaling/v2/namespaces/default/horizontalpodautoscalers/test-hpa" | jq

bytes
Memory is displayed with an incorrect m suffix
Example: 171502796800 bytes = 163,599 MiB Shown incorrectly as 171502796800m

title: apiserver healthz should check etcd override endpoints

### What happened?

But after the bootstrap completes, if the etcd override endpoint become unhealthy, the apiserver health check will still report OK while `kubectl get cs` will report etcd override endpoint is not healthy.

title: bug: kubelet panic & crash if `--config-dir` is used
description:
### What happened?

I created a v1.30.0 k8s cluster with kubeadm and created a  drop-in directory for kubelet configuration under `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d`. The normal conf file created by kubeadm is in ` /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`

According to the [docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubelet-config-file/#kubelet-conf-d) the kubelet should merge all configs in specified order and start. But the kubelet crashes under two setups:

**Setup 1**:

The `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf` is completely empty the kubelet crashes with:
```
>kubelet --config-dir /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d --config /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
E0510 13:47:28.749138    9050 run.go:74] "command failed" err="failed to merge kubelet configs: failed to walk through kubelet dropin directory \"/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d\": failed to load kubelet dropin file, path: /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf, error: kubelet config file \"/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf\" was empty"
```
If there is just one space or an newline in that file it crashes with:
```

        '

Even when the docs say:

> These files may contain partial configurations and might not be valid config files by themselves. Validation is only performed on the final resulting configuration structure stored internally in the kubelet. 

If there is nothing or only whitspaces in  `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d` the merged config should not be invalid and not every file in `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d` must contain a `kind` property.

**Setup 2**:
The `/etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.d/20-kubelet.conf` is the same as the `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` the kubelet panics and crashes with:

title: Custom resource objects can be created during CRD Termination using server-side apply
description:
### What happened?

After a CRD DELETE, while the CRD finalizer is deleting all custom resource objects of that type, and the `Terminating=True` status condition is set, it should not be possible to create objects of that type, but it is with server-side apply, because the creation prevention implementation blocks by method type and there's no check in the PATCH handler.

- CREATE is blocked: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L373
- PATCH is not blocked: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/customresource_handler.go#L390

In the Patch Apply handler, the `forceAllowCreate` flag is set to `true`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/patch.go#L646 This allows patching to always create objects.

### What did you expect to happen?

When the CRD is terminating, SSA should not be able to create new objects.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. apply a CRD
2. apply a CR with a manual finalizer to block CRD termination
3. delete the CRD
4. create a new CR with SSA

### Anything else we need to know?

There is another race condition allowing creation, but it's otherwise unrelated to this bug, which is not a race condition: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/99181

title: NoExecute taint is added with extra 5s delay when a Node's ready condition becomes Unknown
description:
### What happened?

When investigating a delay of Pod eviction on unreachable Node, I found it always took 5s longer than the desired duration.
Looking at the timestamps, I found an odd one: the timestamp when `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` NoExecute taint was added.

```
# Node taints:
taints:
- effect: NoSchedule
  key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
  timeAdded: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
- effect: NoExecute
  key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
  timeAdded: "2023-09-21T06:32:46Z"    # This one is 5s later than all other timestamps

# Node conditions:
conditions:
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: MemoryPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: DiskPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: PIDPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: Ready

# Pod conditions:
- lastProbeTime: null
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  status: "False"
  type: Ready
```

This can be reproducd consistently by terminating kubelet on a Node. The 5s delay of tainting adds 5s delay to the recovery time of Pods which are supposed to be evicted by the taint and recreated on other Nodes sooner. And I can't think of a reason why this taint alone should be added 5s later after the other taint and all other status changes. After investigating the relevant code for how the 5s is introduced, I think it should be an unwanted effect:

`processTaintBaseEviction()` uses the last observed ready condition of the Node instead of the current one to determine whether it should add the Node to the taint queue. When a Node is set to unreachable due to missing heartbeats, the last observed ready condition is still `true` and the current ready condition is `unknown`, we should use the latter for `processTaintBaseEviction()`. Otherwise the taint can only be added when `monitorNodeHealth()` runs another time (5s later) during which the current ready condition becomes the last observed ready condition, like the following logs show:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cde6a46a483a0cc7d3f2404db506e1c24ecd4e9d/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L741

```
# First round handling when the Node is detected as unreachable.
I0921 13:38:27.930549       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="40.006646215s" nodeConditionType=Ready currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:Ready,Status:True,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:KubeletReady,Message:kubelet is posting ready status,}"
I0921 13:38:27.930777       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="40.006732434s" nodeConditionType=MemoryPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:MemoryPressure,Status:False,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:KubeletHasSufficientMemory,Message:kubelet has sufficient memory available,}"
I0921 13:38:27.930881       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="40.006958941s" nodeConditionType=DiskPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:DiskPressure,Status:False,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:KubeletHasNoDiskPressure,Message:kubelet has no disk pressure,}"
I0921 13:38:27.930931       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="40.007072433s" nodeConditionType=PIDPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:PIDPressure,Status:False,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:KubeletHasSufficientPID,Message:kubelet has sufficient PID available,}"
I0921 13:38:27.940640       1 controller_utils.go:186] "Recording status change event message for node" status="NodeNotReady" node="kind-worker2"
I0921 13:38:27.940700       1 controller_utils.go:123] "Update ready status of pods on node" node="kind-worker2"
I0921 13:38:27.940803       1 controller_utils.go:144] "Updating ready status of pod to false" pod="kube-system/antrea-agent-sw57p"
I0921 13:38:27.941226       1 event.go:307] "Event occurred" object="kind-worker2" fieldPath="" kind="Node" apiVersion="v1" type="Normal" reason="NodeNotReady" message="Node kind-worker2 status is now: NodeNotReady"
I0921 13:38:27.952517       1 controller_utils.go:144] "Updating ready status of pod to false" pod="kube-system/kube-proxy-ktsph"
I0921 13:38:27.952879       1 event.go:307] "Event occurred" object="kube-system/antrea-agent-sw57p" fieldPath="" kind="Pod" apiVersion="v1" type="Warning" reason="NodeNotReady" message="Node is not ready"
I0921 13:38:27.961405       1 event.go:307] "Event occurred" object="kube-system/kube-proxy-ktsph" fieldPath="" kind="Pod" apiVersion="v1" type="Warning" reason="NodeNotReady" message="Node is not ready"
# Second round handling after the Node is detected as unreachable.
I0921 13:38:32.962342       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="45.038461632s" nodeConditionType=Ready currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:Ready,Status:Unknown,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:38:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:NodeStatusUnknown,Message:Kubelet stopped posting node status.,}"
I0921 13:38:32.962379       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="45.038523697s" nodeConditionType=MemoryPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:MemoryPressure,Status:Unknown,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:38:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:NodeStatusUnknown,Message:Kubelet stopped posting node status.,}"
I0921 13:38:32.962408       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="45.038548769s" nodeConditionType=DiskPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:DiskPressure,Status:Unknown,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:38:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:NodeStatusUnknown,Message:Kubelet stopped posting node status.,}"
I0921 13:38:32.962431       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:954] "Node hasn't been updated" node="kind-worker2" duration="45.03857838s" nodeConditionType=PIDPressure currentCondition="&NodeCondition{Type:PIDPressure,Status:Unknown,LastHeartbeatTime:2023-09-21 13:35:27 +0000 UTC,LastTransitionTime:2023-09-21 13:38:27 +0000 UTC,Reason:NodeStatusUnknown,Message:Kubelet stopped posting node status.,}"
# The node is added to the taint queue only in the second round.
I0921 13:38:32.962509       1 node_lifecycle_controller.go:793] "Node is unresponsive. Adding it to the Taint queue" node="kind-worker2" timeStamp="2023-09-21 13:38:32.962484274 +0000 UTC m=+71.367258065"
```

I will create a PR to fix it if the above analysis makes sense.

### What did you expect to happen?

`node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` NoExecute taint shouldn't be added with extra 5s delay, compared with when `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` NoSchedule taint is added and the Node is detected as unhealthy.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Stop kubelet on one Node.
2. Check the timestamps of the taints and condition transition of the Node.

title: Deployment names can be too long, such that ReplicaSet creation fails

comments.text: hey @thockin I'm new to k8s ,but i want to try fix this issue. If the deployment name with the replicaset suffix is longer than 253 characters, or the deployment name with the pod suffix is longer than 253 characters, truncate the deployment name and trigger a warning. Do you think logic is right?

I think there are a couple ways this could be approached, which need some consideration.  Off the top of my head:

1) Require that Deployment's name be less than 242 (253 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-') characters.  This seems like a breaking change, but no deployment with that name could ever actually WORK, so acceptable.

2) Accept long names but internally truncate to 242 when creating the replicaset(s).  This leaves room for the replicaset suffix, but that will again be truncated when the pod is created with `generateName`, which only uses 63 characters.  This already generates a warning, so maybe OK?  This will break anyone who tries to parse the RS name and extract the deployment name.

3) Accept long names but internally truncate to fit `generateName` (e.g. 46 (63 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-' - 6 for pod random suffix) when creating the replicaset(s). This will break anyone who tries to parse the RS name and extract the deployment name.

4) Just issue a warning when the name will result in failure (I dislike this option).

No matter what you do, there's a potential for clients who depend on undefined behavior.  For example, they parse out the last `-.{5}` of the pod name to get the replicaset name, and the last `-.{10}` to get the deployment name.  For very long names they will be broken, but they kind of are broken already.

There are almost certainly other options that make different/better tradeoffs, too!
thinks.

The StatefulSet "..." is invalid: metadata.name: Invalid value: "..." : must be no more than 253 characters

I'm not sure I understand the question - AFAICT StatefuleSet uses `apimachineryvalidation.NameIsDNSLabel` and Deployment uses `apimachineryvalidation.NameIsDNSSubdomain` - statefulset should fail at 63 characters.

Unfortunately, we can't really go back and break users by changing this.  If we think it was a mistake to allow DNS Subdomains, we can add warnings but that's about all.

@alculquicondor I'd like to ask a question. how can i connect sig-apps person and discuss this issue. thinks.
If they don't reply on slack, the best venue is in a SIG meeting. Find details here: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/tree/master/sig-apps

>1. Require that Deployment's name be less than 242 (253 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-') characters. This seems like a breaking change, but no deployment with that name could ever actually WORK, so acceptable.

This seems like the best solution to me as we would not break any working deployments.

>2. Accept long names but internally truncate to 242 when creating the replicaset(s).
>3. Accept long names but internally truncate to fit generateName
>
>This will break anyone who tries to parse the RS name and extract the deployment name.

Even though the recommended approach for matching the Deployments and ReplicaSets is OwnerReferences or Labels, we cannot be sure that people are not using the quick and dirty approach of checking for just the name only (e.g. in scripts, tests).

If we go with solution 2 or 3, we will also miss  an opportunity to make the admission validation stricter (solution 1.)

>> 1. Require that Deployment's name be less than 242 (253 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-') characters.
>
> This seems like the best solution to me as we would not break any working deployments.

This is the least impactful change, but I think it's still less than ideal.  Just to be really clear, even ignoring the outright failure mode I reported initially, it is bad in other cases:

What happens today with a long name:
* Create deployment `<59 chars name>`
* Creates RS `<59 chars name>-<10 char hash>`
* Creates pods `<58 chars (truncated)><5 char random>` - note, the hash is totally gone

It's impossible to parse that into either Deployment name or ReplicaSet name.  Both have been obscured.  Worse, if you happen to have 2 long-name Deployments which are the same initial 58 characters, the pods are indistinguishable by name.

But also:
* Create deployment `<48 chars name>`
* Creates RS `<48 chars name>-<10 char hash>`
* Creates pods `<48 chars name>-<9 char hash (truncated)><5 char random>`

At 48 characters, the deployment name survives, but the hash is obscured, so RS name is lost.

This is why I sort of lean to option 3, personally - the pod name includes the whole RS name, but the RS name is a truncated form of the deployment.  I think that's a better tradeoff because humans look at pod names more than RS names, and grouping matters, so optimizing for the better pod names is better.  But I can sort of buy the argument for option 1 too.

> What happens today with a long name:
>    Creates pods <58 chars (truncated)><5 char random> - note, the hash is totally gone

Do users care more about persisting Deployment - RS pairing, or RS - Pod pairing? I agree, it would look better to persist RS - Pod pairing.

Nevertheless this would only get fixed for deployments. Anyone creating replicas manually or by other means, will break the consistency. So you cannot be sure that you can always pair the Pod back to RS, which reduces the benefit a bit. Which you can do with Deployment - RS pairing now, except for the extremely long case.

Certainly needs to be discussed in a SIG meeting. If people think the risk of breaking someone is low, we can do option 3.  We could also do option 1 and 3 at the same time to trim the allowed names a bit.

> Nevertheless this would only get fixed for deployments. Anyone creating replicas manually or by other means, will break the consistency. So you cannot be sure that you can always pair the Pod back to RS

This is true - we can only fix the parts we control, and we don't have a general "append to the name" model because it's complex to design something really useful and because parsing the name is (in general) an anti-pattern.  We know that a pod could be orphaned from an RS/Deployment and adopted by another.  At that point, the pod's name is a staight-up LIE.  :)

It's unfortunate that Deployment becomes aware of RelicaSet's implementation details (i.e. if RS didn't use `generateName`, we'd be having a different discussion!).  Ideally, Deployment would just make totally random RS names, and RS would make totally random pod names, and nobody would parse them - not in code and not visually.  But that's a crappy human UX for the most common path.

> I think there are a couple ways this could be approached, which need some consideration. Off the top of my head:
> 
> 1. Require that Deployment's name be less than 242 (253 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-') characters.  This seems like a breaking change, but no deployment with that name could ever actually WORK, so acceptable.
> 2. Accept long names but internally truncate to 242 when creating the replicaset(s).  This leaves room for the replicaset suffix, but that will again be truncated when the pod is created with `generateName`, which only uses 63 characters.  This already generates a warning, so maybe OK?  This will break anyone who tries to parse the RS name and extract the deployment name.
> 3. Accept long names but internally truncate to fit `generateName` (e.g. 46 (63 - 10 for hash - 1 for '-' - 6 for pod random suffix) when creating the replicaset(s). This will break anyone who tries to parse the RS name and extract the deployment name.
> 4. Just issue a warning when the name will result in failure (I dislike this option).

@thockin Sig apps think option 1 would be better.

So if we pursued option 1, Deployments would have shorter names, ReplicaSets would have long names, and Pods would have gibberish names.  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116447#issuecomment-1496210300

Is that really well understood?  I am a little surprised, personally, but OK.

Should we take this as an opportunity to update docs to express that the name-relationship between Deployment -> RS -> Pod is NOT part of the API contract, and should not be depended on?

I'm curious, truncating does not look great does it?
so I have my deployment in my manifest with name 250 chars "superlong........name12345678" and when I try to check I can only use it with the truncated name of 242 chars, no? kubectl get deployment "superlong...name"

Sorry. It may be I didn't make them understand well. They may think option 1 is the simplest way and won't bring some breaking.

yes. When deployment name length is longer than 242, return fail. But option 3 looks more nice and breaking is

If we did 3, there's no need for 1.

To be clear: I think 3 is superior to 1, but I am not going to fight too hard for it.  I think it's a better human UX, but it does make the set of RS whose names can be parsed to a Deployment smaller.  It doesn't change the set of Pods whose name can be parsed.  Parsing names is dirty, in general.

To recap, what happens today:

## A) Deployment names less than 48 characters are fine.

## B) Deployment names of 48-58 characters are awkward:
  Create deployment `<48 chars name>`
    Creates RS `<48 chars name>-<10 char hash>` - can be parsed for deployment name
      Creates pods `<48 chars name>-<9 char hash (truncated)><5 char random>` - cannot be parsed to RS or deployment name

## C) Deployment names of 243+ characters break totally:
  Create deployment `<243 chars name>`
    Fail to create RS `<243 chars name>-<10 char hash>`

Solution 1 (seemingly decided) changes case C to API fail the deployment creation - which is easier to catch.  It is identical behavior in case B.

Solution 3 changes case B into:

## B') Deployment names of 47-253 characters break gently:
  Create deployment `<47 chars name>`
    Creates RS `<46 chars name>-<10 char hash>` - cannot be parsed for deployment name
      Creates pods `<46 chars name>-<10 char hash>-<5 char random>` - cannot be parsed to RS or deployment name

The main distinction being that the RS hash is preserved (good for humans), but  Deployment names of 47-242 characters can not have their RS names parsed (bad for machines). 

Again, parsing names is dirty, in general.  But that doesn't mean people don't do it!

@janetkuo @kow3ns @soltysh - if you confirm the decision, I'll STFU :)

Why does generateName limit to only 63 characters, if Pod name limit is 253?

To recap on ability to parse: users can parse a Deployment name from any Replicaset name, but they cannot parse either Deployment or Replicaset names from a Pod name, reliably.

To break or not to break :thinking:

See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/64023#issuecomment-1531459619 for a related discussion, where we decided not to change validation.

generateName doesn't really know which underlying resource it is using or
the rules for it, so it assumes the baseline.

That said, Pod names > 63 is a problem because of 'hostname'.

If we are ok with breaking users that might be parsing a Deployment name from a ReplicaSet name, then I'm ok with solution 3. I wouldn't expect there to be many, as opposed to ones trying to parse a Deployment name from Pod, which is already broken.

What do we gain? The ability to create working Deployments with slightly longer names, which might be useful.

> So there is no world where we can make Pod from ReplicaSets have longer
names

Well, RS doesn't *have to* use generateName, it's just convenient.  It
could generate names itself (as does deployment).  But any pod name > 63
will be weird for hostname, so we recommend not to do that (API warning).

I wish we had just kept it simple all along. :)

from a ReplicaSet name, then I'm ok with solution 3. I wouldn't expect

Pod, which is already broken

Keep in mind that for "reasonable" names (less than 40ish) this is all

The [Deployment doc ](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/) said:

title: Kubelet should enforce that static pods do not reference other API objects
description:
#### What happened:
I put into `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` one defining a static pod with a `serviceAccount`, because I was wondering if this is supported (the documentation does not say, see https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/28611#issuecomment-876537379).  The kubelet created the pod but without giving it the relevant mount.  The kubelet did _not_ create the corresponding mirror pod.

Here is the manifest I created:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test5
spec:
  containers:
  - name: bb
    image: busybox
    command:
    - sleep
    - "864001"
  serviceAccountName: default
```
Here are some relevant log entries from the kubelet:
```
Jul 08 15:55:05 init1 kubelet[4229]: I0708 15:55:05.335792    4229 kubelet.go:1681] "Creating a mirror pod for static pod" pod="default/test5-init1"

Jul 08 15:55:05 init1 kubelet[4229]: E0708 15:55:05.343771    4229 kubelet.go:1683] "Failed creating a mirror pod for" err="pods \"test5-init1\" is forbidden: a mirror pod may not reference service accounts" pod="default/test5-init1"
```

#### What you expected to happen:
I expected consistent treatment --- real pod and mirror pod both exist or both do not exist.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
I think the above is pretty minimal.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
  ```
  Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"21", GitVersion:"v1.21.1", GitCommit:"5e58841cce77d4bc13713ad2b91fa0d961e69192", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-05-12T14:18:45Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.4", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
   Server Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"21", GitVersion:"v1.21.2", GitCommit:"092fbfbf53427de67cac1e9fa54aaa09a28371d7", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-06-16T12:53:14Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.5", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
  ```
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: VirtualBox x86_64 VMs with 2 virtual CPUs and 2 GB of memory
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): Ubuntu 20.04.1 LTS
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): `Linux init1 5.4.0-65-generic #73-Ubuntu SMP Mon Jan 18 17:25:17 UTC 2021 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
- Install tools: kubeadm v1.21.2
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:

comments.text: @kubernetes/sig-node-bugs

It is expected that static pod will not run... no references to API objects are permitted in static pods (service accounts, PVC objects, secrets, configmaps, etc). 

> The kubelet created the pod but without giving it the relevant mount. The kubelet did not create the corresponding mirror pod.

I'm not sure I understand what you mean by this

Ooh, the prohibition is even broader.  @liggitt please have a look at https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/28623 and there should probably also be updates to PodSpec and/or types inside it.

As for what I meant: the kubelet implemented the pod:
```
root@init1:~# docker ps
CONTAINER ID   IMAGE                    COMMAND                  CREATED             STATUS             PORTS     NAMES
c87ee60d1f92   busybox                  "sleep 864001"           About an hour ago   Up About an hour             k8s_bb_test5-init1_default_595a2ca0aaa264ec6f10330a8d5162a8_0
6c885e29da59   k8s.gcr.io/pause:3.4.1   "/pause"                 About an hour ago   Up About an hour             k8s_POD_test5-init1_default_595a2ca0aaa264ec6f10330a8d5162a8_0
...
```

but the mirror pod object did not get created in the apiserver.
Definitely seems like a bug that we actually run that - given that we can never report it to the API.
(valid bug that is unlikely to be fixed by accident)
xref: [REDACTED]
Adding SIG storage since volume mounts outside of host path and empty dir do not make sense for static pods.
xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/website/pull/28623 https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/28611 #103167

the HEAD commit at https://github.com/liggitt/kubernetes/commits/kubelet-static-api-reference is a sketch of what this could look like, catching API references in file and url sourced pods and preventing them from ever being handled by the kubelet
Agreed this should be blocked at creation time
Is this enforced at API today?  Is there any backward compatibility implication to tightening Kubelet validation?

> Is this enforced at API today?

Yes, NodeRestriction admission blocks the serviceaccount/secret/configmap/pvc references that would inform node authorizer:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0270fc75d0f59e1f5a31a810737ac35ac3eeb8a3/plugin/pkg/admission/noderestriction/admission.go#L247-L265

Blocking pod creation there means the node is silently running static pods that *probably* aren't working (API references that require authz fail unless another pod on the same node happens to reference the same API object), and *definitely* are confusing the scheduler because the resources they consume aren't represented in the API.

> Is there any backward compatibility implication to tightening Kubelet validation?

A kubelet could conceivably be running static pods whose referenced resources *happened* to also be referenced by a non-static pod on the same node, but that doesn't seem like it would result in consistently successful pods.
xref [REDACTED] which is adding another API reference field to protect against in static / mirror pods

We need some advisement on how to proceed with this. changes like this create backwards compatibility issues. It's possible we shouldn't address this in tree, and maybe recommend a daemonset or something that edits the manifests. Either way, we need some guidance and probably can't decide this alone

> We need some advisement on how to proceed with this. changes like this create backwards compatibility issues. It's possible we shouldn't address this in tree, and maybe recommend a daemonset or something that edits the manifests. Either way, we need some guidance and probably can't decide this alone

This issue seems like a bug and the created static pods may not be working 100% anyway. 
If we want to be extra careful, we could try one of the following routes:
 - Add a warning but not fail for one release to raise awareness; fail the validation in the next release
 - Fail the validation, but add a temporary flag to restore the old behavior to tie user over for a release or two (of course then we'll have to remove the flag later). 
 
WDYT? @haircommander

> Fail the validation, but add a temporary flag to restore the old behavior to tie user over for a release or two (of course then we'll have to remove the flag later).

That's what I would expect. Fix the validation gap, make the tightened validation able to be opted out of with a feature gate marked as deprecated for a release or two

title: conversion-gen generates code that leads to panics when fields are accessed after conversion
description:
### What happened?

As the title says, conversion-gen has a bug that generates incorrect conversion code.

struct in the old apiVersion:
```go
type JSONSchemaProps struct {
	Items      *JSONSchemaProps           `json:"items,omitempty"`
	Properties map[string]JSONSchemaProps `json:"properties,omitempty"`
	AllOf      []JSONSchemaProps          `json:"allOf,omitempty"`

	ExclusiveMaximum bool `json:"exclusiveMaximum,omitempty"`
}
```

struct in the new apiVersion: (`ExclusiveMaximum` was changed from `bool` to `*bool`)
```go
type JSONSchemaProps struct {
	Items      *JSONSchemaProps           `json:"items,omitempty"`
	Properties map[string]JSONSchemaProps `json:"properties,omitempty"`
	AllOf      []JSONSchemaProps          `json:"allOf,omitempty"`

	ExclusiveMaximum *bool `json:"exclusiveMaximum,omitempty"`
}
```

Generated conversion code:
```go
func autoConvert_v1beta2_JSONSchemaProps_To_v1beta1_JSONSchemaProps(in *v1beta2.JSONSchemaProps, out *JSONSchemaProps, s conversion.Scope) error {
	out.Items = (*JSONSchemaProps)(unsafe.Pointer(in.Items))
	out.Properties = *(*map[string]JSONSchemaProps)(unsafe.Pointer(&in.Properties))
	out.AllOf = *(*[]JSONSchemaProps)(unsafe.Pointer(&in.AllOf))
	if err := v1.Convert_Pointer_bool_To_bool(&in.ExclusiveMaximum, &out.ExclusiveMaximum, s); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return nil
}
```

Issue: 
`out.Items = (*JSONSchemaProps)(unsafe.Pointer(in.Items))` is wrong (similar for `Properties` and `AllOf`).
`autoConvert_v1beta2_JSONSchemaProps_To_v1beta1_JSONSchemaProps` should be called instead.

Accessing the `ExlusiveMaximum` field after conversion leads to a panic.

Full example can be seen here: https://github.com/sbueringer/conversion-gen-panic-repro (just checkout and run `make test`).

### What did you expect to happen?

conversion-gen should generate correct code

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Full example can be seen here: https://github.com/sbueringer/conversion-gen-panic-repro (just checkout and run `make test`).

### Kubernetes version

conversion-gen v0.33.0

Related Slack thread: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C0EG7JC6T/p1752170662367799 (but all relevant information is contained in this issue)

comments.text: Thanks for the detailed reproducer. This is a bug in equalMemoryTypes#equal `alreadyVisitedTypes` handling that short-circuited type comparison on a guard intended to prevent infinite recursion, but which assumes any already-visited type in the stack is equal. When there are recursively defined types, this is not always the case.
opened [REDACTED] with an in-tree example reproducer of the types which trigger the logic error... working on a fix

Validation-gen has to jump through significant hoops to handle recursion in types, too.

did you know that `type T []T` is valid in Go?  :)
fix pushed to [REDACTED]

title: kube-proxy error when loadBalancerSourceRanges have zero-masked cidr
description:

title: kube-proxy incorrectly logs "Ignoring same-zone topology hints" when there are no endpoints
description:
### What happened?

We recently upgraded our EKS cluster from 1.32 to 1.33, and noticed an unusually high volume of logs coming from kube-proxy like this:
```
Ignoring same-zone topology hints for service since no hints were provided for zone
```

We have not enabled zone-aware routing or hints (either by .spec.trafficDistribution or by the older annotation) for any service and were surprised to see this log message. The service has no endpoints in the endpoint slice.

<details>
<summary> Example service YAML</summary>

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-service
  namespace: default
spec:
  clusterIP: 10.10.129.215
  clusterIPs:
  - 10.10.129.215
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ipFamilies:
  - IPv4
  ipFamilyPolicy: SingleStack
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 80
  selector:
    app: my-service
  sessionAffinity: None
  type: ClusterIP
status:
  loadBalancer: {}
```

</details>

<details>
<summary> Example endpointslice YAML</summary>

```yaml
addressType: IPv4
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
endpoints: null
kind: EndpointSlice
metadata:
  annotations:
    endpoints.kubernetes.io/last-change-trigger-time: "2024-10-29T09:45:37Z"
  creationTimestamp: "2024-10-11T12:46:31Z"
  generateName: my-service-
  generation: 397
  labels:
    endpointslice.kubernetes.io/managed-by: endpointslice-controller.k8s.io
  name: my-service-qwq6l
  namespace: default
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: v1
    blockOwnerDeletion: true
    controller: true
    kind: Service
    name: my-service
    uid: 2c3edd43-8041-4aa6-ac2b-8e5508d7c6ff
  resourceVersion: "5958818965"
  uid: b485a7f7-6363-4b5f-b3f2-d6eb394ac034
ports: null
```

</details>

Looking through [topology.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/proxy/topology.go#L195), it looks like we intend to log this line when all endpoints in the endpoint slice have zone hints, and the zone parameter is not empty. However, since we initialise allEndpointsHaveZoneHints to true then loop through the endpoints to set it to false, we will inadvertently log this line for any endpoint slices that are empty.

I think the simple fix is to exit `topologyModeFromHints` early and return an empty string if no endpoints are found. I am happy to contribute this patch

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect to not see this log line for empty endpoint slices

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I have not tried it, but I presume you could create a service with no endpoints and see that kube-proxy logs this log line

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: [PodLevelResources] Update Downward API defaulting logic for `resource.limits`
description:
Using the Downward API's [resourceFieldRef](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/downward-api/#downwardapi-resourcefieldref), you can inject values specified in `resources.limits`, such as CPU, memory, or ephemeral storage into environment variables.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: downward-api-resource-limits
spec:
  containers:
  - name: sleep
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "echo CPU_LIMIT=$CPU_LIMIT; echo MEMORY_LIMIT=$MEMORY_LIMIT; sleep infinity"]
    resources:
      limits:
        cpu: 500m
        memory: 128Mi
    env:
    - name: CPU_LIMIT
      valueFrom:
        resourceFieldRef:
          resource: limits.cpu
    - name: MEMORY_LIMIT
      valueFrom:
        resourceFieldRef:
          resource: limits.memory
```

Currently, when container-level resource limits were not specified and the Downward API was used to set environment variables referencing them, the node's allocatable resources were used in the defaulting logic.
With the introduction of the Pod Level Resources feature, this behavior should be updated as outlined in the comment.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b2f27c0649fc0f3d2a4a6dd29135ecc81781f7e4/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_resources.go#L33-L34

title: [PodLevelResources] Validation for Windows OS
description:
PodLevelResources feature is not supported on Windows OS. Add the necessary validation logic to reject pods for Windows.

From the KEP #2837, until full Windows support for pod-level resource specifications is implemented, the behavior for pods, with pod-level resources, targeting Windows is as follows:

- API Server Validation: If the spec.os.name field in the Pod specification is explicitly set to "windows", the Kubernetes API server will generally reject the pod during validation.

    Add the following logic in [validatePodResources](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c14c5722a2e8f357dac32be1e1018925b05158e0/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L4302)
       // windows pods are not supported.
	if oldPod.Spec.OS != nil && oldPod.Spec.OS.Name == core.Windows && pod level resources are set {
		return field.ErrorList....
	}

- Kubelet Admission: The Kubelet running on a Windows node would reject the pod, with pod-level resources, during admission.
     
     Add IsPodLevelResourcesAllowed in features_windows.go, features_linux.go and features_unsupported.go (example - [ref](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Akubernetes%2Fkubernetes+%22func+IsInPlacePodVerticalScalingAllowed%22&type=code)  
    and call this method from [SyncPod](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1680008ddc74dc7141a4c26fa17b99d5dde99d4d/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_manager.go#L1134)) if pod level resources are set in the spec

title: [Pod Level Resources] Pod-level resource validation fails when container-level is set for other resource
description:
### What happened?

When a Kubernetes Pod defines resources.requests at the Pod level, but only specifies a subset of the supported resources requested by its containers (e.g., only cpu at the Pod level, while a container requests memory), Kubernetes' validation implicitly assigns a request of "0" for the unstated resource (e.g., memory) at the Pod level. This "0" value then triggers a validation error because it's less than the actual aggregated request from the containers, even though the user might expect the Pod to implicitly aggregate the container's memory request.

```
 "pod" is invalid: spec.resources.requests[memory]: Invalid value: "0": must be greater than or equal to aggregate container requests of 10Mi
```

### What did you expect to happen?

When a user defines resource requests at the container level, Kubernetes already aggregates these requests internally to determine the total resource needs of the Pod. If the Pod.spec.resources.requests field is present, but only specifies a subset of resources (e.g., cpu but not memory), the intuitive expectation is that Kubernetes would implicitly aggregate the memory request from the containers, rather than defaulting the Pod's memory request to 0.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ccf291b50166ce82204486aae6a626a30b469182/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L4406 needs to be fixed to compare container aggregates with pod-level values only if pod-level value for that resource is set.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Enable PodLevelResources feature gate on apiserver, scheduler and kubelet, and create the following pod
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pod-bug
spec:
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: "300m"  # Pod-level CPU request
  containers:
  - name: sleep-infinity
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep infinity"]
    resources:
      requests:
        ephemeral-memory: 10Mi 
```

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.33.1

title: `kube_codegen.sh` does not resolve "local" GOBIN when invoking the tools
description:
### What happened?

Required binaries are installed using `go install`, which relies on the predefined `GOBIN`. But when codegen tools are invoked in the script, the resolved `gobin` variable might not be pointing to the right location, as it's only resolving the environment variable (`$GOBIN`) or fall back to `$GOPATH/bin` explicitly, missing the value which might be set for `go env GOBIN` without exporting it.

### What did you expect to happen?

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

❯ go env -w GOBIN=$(mktemp -d)

I am experiencing the same issue.

FYI:
- To reproduce that issue with `kubectl` command, you must use `kubectl create`, not `kubectl apply`.
- This bug happens at `1.33` release.
    - `1.33.0`, `1.33.1`, and `1.33.2` have same issue.
    - It does not happen before `1.33` release.

@liubog2008 why do you want to configure/create `default/kubernetes` service?
It is managed by a controller k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controlplane/controller/kubernetesservice

> POST an existing service. A new ip address will be created and then cleaned up.

@aroradaman  I think that is an example to demonstrate the problem.

What happens is that the IPAddress is created but later in the process the Service creation fails, but the IP cleanup races with the repairip loop `repairip.go` and emits the event, then the `ipallocator.go` fails to delete the address because is already removed.

```
I0624 21:36:16.957221       1 cidrallocator.go:277] updated ClusterIP allocator for Service CIDR 10.96.0.0/16
E0624 21:38:08.604887       1 repairip.go:523] "Unhandled Error" err="the IPAddress: 10.96.26.13 for Service kubernetes/default has a wrong reference &v1.ParentReference{Group:\"\", Resource:\"services\", Namespace:\"default\", Name:\"kubernetes\"}; cleaning up" logger="UnhandledError"
I0624 21:38:08.610759       1 ipallocator.go:374] error releasing ip 10.96.26.13 : ipaddresses.networking.k8s.io "10.96.26.13" not found
I0624 21:38:08.614075       1 cidrallocator.go:277] updated ClusterIP allocator for Service CIDR 10.96.0.0/16
E0624 21:38:14.667918       1 repairip.go:523] "Unhandled Error" err="the IPAddress: 10.96.104.42 for Service kubernetes/default has a wrong reference &v1.ParentReference{Group:\"\", Resource:\"services\", Namespace:\"default\", Name:\"kubernetes\"}; cleaning up" logger="UnhandledError"
I0624 21:38:14.670970       1 cidrallocator.go:277] updated ClusterIP allocator for Service CIDR 10.96.0.0/16
I0624 21:38:14.671700       1 ipallocator.go:374] error releasing ip 10.96.104.42 : ipaddresses.networking.k8s.io "10.96.104.42" not found
```

so the IP allocated is WAI, it worked that way before, it seems the only problem is that is emitting an event, or are there any other issues @liubog2008 ?

> so the IP allocated is WAI, it worked that way before, it seems the only problem is that is emitting an event, or are there any other issues [@liubog2008](https://github.com/liubog2008) ?

@aojea In my case, there are no other issues. (Event emitting is the only problem)

Below are the details in my case:
- I am implementing operator, which has a `Service` creation logic.
- It does not check existance of the target `Service` when creating it, and just ignores "Already Exists" error.
- As operator periodically executes the reconcile loop, error `Event` emitting happens repeatedly.

> @liubog2008 why do you want to configure/create default/kubernetes service?

@aroradaman Just an example for easily reproducing.
@aojea I think the problem is when I try to create an existing service, apiserver should reject the request and not create anything.
My use case is same as @hoony9x

> [@aojea](https://github.com/aojea) I think the problem is when I try to create an existing service, apiserver should reject the request and not create anything.

Service is the only API that implement a transaction and uses the IPAddress object to guarantee consistency across the cluster,  you can read more in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/1880-multiple-service-cidrs/README.md

The allocation of the IP happens first, and if the service creation fails, the IP is deleted, is an internal operation, if you see the log when the Service fails to be created the transaction is reverted ...  the repair loop is faster and emits an event. In this case the problem is that the Service already exist, so the repair loop does not wait for the transaction to finish and removes the IP because checks that the ClusterIP of the Service does not match the object, hence it is a leak

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec80dcaf3892d0cf89e4fd7b1ea60300fb417d8a/pkg/registry/core/service/ipallocator/controller/repairip.go#L492-L529

The problem is that we should not try to allocate an IP address for a Service that already exists and has IPs allocated, and fail at that moment ... but Service pipeline is complex and allocation happens at `BeginCreate`, @thockin @liggitt do you know if we can detect that at this stage?

> in version 1.33+, the resource `ip` created and then deleted.

that is not a problem, those resources are owned by the apiserver so it is ok

> can this be solved by adding a judgment in BeginCreate

does not looks like a great pattern to implement, and can be also racy, in multiple master environment, services can be created/deleted/updated in parallel

> does not looks like a great pattern to implement, and can be also racy, in multiple master environment, services can be created/deleted/updated in parallel

I think it's enough? It can fix most unnecessary ip allocation by a lower cost (create a new ip vs get a svc from cache). And just keep the `repairip` to avoid race.

> The problem is that we should not try to allocate an IP address for a Service that already exists and has IPs allocated, and fail at that moment ... but Service pipeline is complex and allocation happens at `BeginCreate`, [@thockin](https://github.com/thockin) [@liggitt](https://github.com/liggitt) do you know if we can detect that at this stage?

No, trying to detect existence before persisting to etcd ~doubles the cost of creates and makes a new race that can still happen if two creates are attempted simultaneously.

I think it's better to tweak the repair loop to avoid spurious warnings in this scenario... perhaps by doing something like:
* If an IPAddress is observed with a creation timestamp *after* the service it references, delay repair loop processing of the IPAddress for a few seconds (1? 5?) in case the IPAddress was provisioned and then immediately cleaned up as part of a transaction.
Hi, I have tried the fix @liggitt proposed and it is removing the errors. @aroradaman I am happy to open a PR if you haven't already started working on the fix.

Which gRPC endpoint of the podresources API does `knit podres` call?
https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/compute-storage-net/device-plugins/#monitoring-device-plugin-resources
If it’s using `GetAllocatableResources`, it seems like information about `Completed` pods might also be included. Since `List` is supposed to return information only for running pods, including `Completed` pods would seem like a bug.
@toVersus It uses List() function

the problem here is how the podresources API implementation fetches data from the resource managers. Looking at the implementation here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/apis/podresources/server_v1.go#L60 we take care of syncing the device allocation data before querying the resource managers to return their pod->devices assignment. This is needed because otherwise the resource managers would do the cleanup asynchronously, so the `List` call will return incorrect data.

But we don't do this syncing neither for CPUs or for memory, so when we report these we will get stale data as this issue demonstrates.

For CPU manager, we however have the reconcile loop which cleans the stale data periodically. Turns out this timing interplay was actually the reason the existing issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119423 seemed fixed (see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119423#issuecomment-2786891218). But it's actually timing. If in the reproducer we set the `cpuManagerReconcilePeriod` to a time very high (>= 5 minutes), then the issue still reproduces against current master branch (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/podresources_test.go#L983).

We can fix in two ways: adding explicit syncs for cpu and memory like we do for devices.
Or, fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119423 making the `List` endpoint iterate over the active pods (vs all of them). This is the best fix because it makes the endpoint consistent with what the resource managers are doing.
`List` is using all the pods known about: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L3135 -> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/pod/pod_manager.go#L215
But all the resource managers are using the list of active pods: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L1666 -> https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L198

Now: I read the warning in the docstring of GetActivePods and still having the endpoint using a different podset wrt the resource managers with the related desync causes way more harm than good. I can't really see a good reason to. And still, we can and probably should have a way to preserve the old behavior to zero the chance to break users of the API depending on the old behavior

So, we have the following options to fix:

1.    fix the issues with this approach implemented in [REDACTED] 
2.    fix the issue with a different approach: sync the state before each List call, like we do for devices. Still pretty much contained, adds lock contention
3.    option 1, add a feature gate, without a KEP (benefits unclear: all changes here are opt-in anyway)
4.    option 2, add a feature gate, without a KEP
5.    file a new KEP. If we file a new KEP I'd rather propose a new endpoint (ListActive? ListAllocatedResources?) fixing all the known issues of the List endpoint. I really do think this KEP should start beta, as there are no unknowns (and no risks, btw, being a new additive and partially overlapping endpoint)

title: kube-proxy: externalTrafficPolicy:Local and proxy-mode=nftables blackholes pods traffic to external IPs
description:
### What happened?

When using kube-proxy on nftables mode and specify a `LoadBalancer` Service with `externalTrafficPolicy:Local` that has an ExternalIP assigned, kube-proxy will create an entry in the kube-proxy ip nftable that will drop traffic to that external IP, like:

```
        map no-endpoint-services {
                type ipv4_addr . inet_proto . inet_service : verdict
                comment "vmap to drop or reject packets to services with no endpoints"
                elements = { 
                             10.88.1.2 . tcp . 80 comment "sys-ingress-priv/internal-ingress-controller-v2:web" : drop,
```

As a result, any pod on the host cannot send traffic to the external IP of the LoadBalancer.

### What did you expect to happen?

On nodes where no workload is present, traffic should not be dropped but load balanced by kube proxy to the target Service endpoints.
This will also bring consistency with how other modes work, as this issue was addressed both for ipvs (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/93456)
and iptables (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/77523) modes.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run kube-proxy on nftables mode and try hitting a `LoadBalancer` Service `ExternalIP` from within a pod running in a node that does not have ready endpoints of the target service

### Anything else we need to know?

@kubernetes/sig-network-bugs
Simmilar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/75262 but for `nftables` mode

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
Server Version: v1.33.0
```

aws, gcp and bare metal

comments.text: ping @danwinship @aroradaman

I was able to reproduce this for LoadBalancerIPs.
 
We short-circuit traffic originating within the cluster (from pods or workers) that is destined for external addresses (LoadBalancerIP, ExternalIP, or NodePort), DNATing it to cluster endpoints rather than local endpoints.

The filter-output is hooked to output hook with a priority lower than DNAT (-110), and the packets are dropped before the short-circuiting kicks in.
confirmed with trace
```

trace id f97b367d ip kube-proxy service-endpoints-check rule ip daddr . meta l4proto . th dport vmap @no-endpoint-services (verdict drop)
trace id 587493e0 ip filter trace packet: oif "eth0" ip saddr 172.18.0.3 ip daddr 172.18.0.100 ip dscp cs0 ip ecn not-ect ip ttl 64 ip id 53571 ip length 60 tcp sport 53880 tcp dport 3000 tcp flags == syn tcp window 64240

trace id 587493e0 ip filter trace verdict continue

trace id 587493e0 ip kube-proxy filter-output packet: oif "eth0" ip saddr 172.18.0.3 ip daddr 172.18.0.100 ip dscp cs0 ip ecn not-ect ip ttl 64 ip id 53571 ip length 60 tcp sport 53880 tcp dport 3000 tcp flags == syn tcp window 64240 
trace id 587493e0 ip kube-proxy filter-output rule ct state new jump service-endpoints-check (verdict jump service-endpoints-check)
trace id 587493e0 ip kube-proxy service-endpoints-check rule ip daddr . meta l4proto . th dport vmap @no-endpoint-services (verdict drop)
```

@danwinship I tried to set priority of all filter chains to 0 (default filter priority) and handle the firewall-check case which happens in filter-prerouting and filter-output using original destination IP and port from conntrack but it turns out we can not match on `inet_service` data type with `ct original proto-dst` expression.
(ref: https://wiki.nftables.org/wiki-nftables/index.php/Data_types#IP_types)

```
E0622 17:16:35.104974       1 proxier.go:1850] "nftables sync failed" err=<
    /dev/stdin:61:75-97: Error: can not use variable sized data types (invalid) in concat expressions
    add rule ip kube-proxy firewall-check ct original ip daddr . meta l4proto . ct original proto-dst vmap @firewall-ips
                                          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

I was thinking of having `filter-prerouting-pre-dnat` and `filter-output-pre-dnat` chains hooked with -110 priority. These chains  will jump to firewall check. And `filter-input`, `filter-forward`, `filter-output` chains hooked with priority 0. 
We can also merge the `filter-output-post-dnat` into `filter-output` with this change.

> it turns out we can not match on `inet_service` data type with `ct original proto-dst` expression

That error seems wrong... the man page claims that `proto-dst` is a 16-bit integer, so it shouldn't be saying it's "variable sized"... but at any rate, even if it is a bug and they fix it, we can't depend on that fix for a long time.

title: Does the cpu static policy option of PreferAlignByUncoreCache only support even CPU counts?
description:
### What happened?

When I assign an odd number of CPUs and less than a full uncorecache, this policy cannot assign the cpu properly. I do not know if this option only support even number CPU by design or it is a bug.

For example, 1core:2cpus, cache0: 0-8 cpus. If I assign 7cpus in the pod spec, `takePartialUncore` cannot take any cpus.
