title: [Winkernel Proxier] RemoteEndpoint deletion not occurring when Deployment is referenced by multiple Services (stale RemoteEndpoints remain at scale)
description:
### What happened?

When a Deployment is referenced by multiple Services, the associated RemoteEndpoints are sometimes not deleted when the Deployment or Pods are terminated. This leads to the presence of stale RemoteEndpoints in the system.

This issue is observed only in large-scale environments with a high number of Services and Endpoints, suggesting a potential race condition or delayed cleanup in the controller logic.

### What did you expect to happen?

All RemoteEndpoints associated with a Deployment should be deleted once the Deployment or its Pods are removed - regardless of the number of Services referencing it.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create an AKS Cluster with K8S version 1.31.x+ and Windows NodePool
 
- Create a Deployment with multiple replicas.

comments.text: Looking into it now.

It's definitely that commit. Reverting restores performance:

```
                                                                                             │          before.log          │                      after.log                       │
                                                                                             │ SchedulingThroughput/Average │ SchedulingThroughput/Average  vs base                │
PerfScheduling/SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate/empty_500nodes-8                                          85.00 ± 5%                   160.00 ± 12%   +88.24% (p=0.002 n=6)
PerfScheduling/SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate/empty_500nodes_QueueingHintsEnabled-8                     83.03 ± 2%                   173.35 ±  5%  +108.78% (p=0.002 n=6)
PerfScheduling/SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate/half_500nodes-8                                           80.50 ± 1%                   209.75 ±  9%  +160.58% (p=0.002 n=6)
PerfScheduling/SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate/half_500nodes_QueueingHintsEnabled-8                      75.75 ± 3%                   210.00 ±  3%  +177.21% (p=0.002 n=6)
PerfScheduling/SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate/full_500nodes-8                                                                         219.6 ±  2%
PerfScheduling/SteadyStateClusterResourceClaimTemplate/full_500nodes_QueueingHintsEnabled-8                                                    204.8 ±  4%
geomean                                                                                                          81.00                         195.0        +130.82%
```

Yeah, the change is definitely the cause here.

I'm trying to think of ways to address this. So as far as I can tell, there are two ways we can handle this:

1. Determine which pools are incomplete before we start converting them, which allows us to just throw away any slices in the pool that doesn't target the node. The benefit is that we don't have to do any conversion or other handling of those slices, but the drawback is the work needed to determine if the pools are incomplete up front. This is what was implemented in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134466. 

2. The other option is to keep enough state as part of the current loop through the slices so we can determine later if a pool is incomplete. The drawback here is that we need to do this for every pool in the cluster, since we can't know if a pool is relevant for a node without looking at every slice. So in situations where there are a pool per node, we need to keep track of completeness for every pool. I have a quick-and-dirty attempt at this approach in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/master...mortent:DRAPerfImprovement. I haven't run the full perf suite on it, but it seems to have the same performance problems as the merged PR.

This actually becomes an even larger issue for Partitionable Devices. Since we are scoping the counter sets to a pool, the allocator needs to know about all allocated devices that consumes counters in that pool, meaning we need to know about allocated devices on other nodes than the current one.

I'm wondering if an option here is to say that all ResourceSlices in a pool must have the same node selector? The resourceslice-controller kinda already enforces this since it only allows specifying the NodeSelector on the Pool level:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/afb2b97425317948e9e59b2a7871fca5bbb2ab08/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/resourceslice/resourceslicecontroller.go#L128-L153

For `PerDeviceNodeSelection` things gets a bit more complicated, but we could still require that all slices in the pool use the same node selector. This would allow the allocator to throw away slices that doesn't target the current node, knowing that no slices in the pool will target the node and therefore we don't care about whether the slice is complete. But it can't be validated on admission and validating it in the allocator would be expensive.

Both [REDACTED] and  [REDACTED] fix this based on the idea from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/135032#issuecomment-3476686304, but the latter is a bit simpler and has more test cases.

title: ResourceClaim strategy test miss the unexpected error check
description:
### What happened?

According to the comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134615#discussion_r2475964555 by @mortent, the assertion in `pkg/registry/resource/resourceclaimtemplate/strategy_test.go` doesn't catch situations where Validate unexpectedly returns errors.

Since tc.expectValidationError is an empty string in this situation, it will pass. It should check that if tc.expectValidationError is an empty string, the length of errs should be zero.

After adding the suggestion, I found a couple of errors reported including immutable fields from DRAConsumableCapacity and DRADeviceBindingConditions.

After fixing the immutable fields, I further encounter the error of drop field test cases in DRADeviceBindingConditions and it seems that the drop field function is not implemented yet.

### What did you expect to happen?

```
Test assertion should detect unexpected error (tc.expectValidationError="" but len(errs) != 0)
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Add

```diff
                        if errs := strategy.Validate(ctx, obj); len(errs) != 0 {

+                               }
                                assert.ErrorContains(t, errs[0], tc.expectValidationError, "the error message should have contained the expected error message")
```

title: (DRA) Requests field not set for config FromClass in ResourceClaim.status.allocation.devices.config
description:
### What happened?

When creating a ResourceClaim with 2 requests with 2 different device class that have a config, the config reported in the allocation devices status is not mentioning from which request the config is coming from. So the DRA-Drivers cannot identify the configuration belonging to the request it is supposed to handle.
```yaml
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: my-resource-claim
spec:
...
status:
  allocation:
    devices:
      config:
      - opaque:
          driver: resource-driver.example.com
          parameters:
            test: example-0
        source: FromClass
      - opaque:
          driver: resource-driver.example.com
          parameters:
            test: example-1
        source: FromClass
      results:
      - device: eth0
        driver: resource-driver.example.com
        pool: kind-worker2
        request: request0
      - device: eth1
        driver: resource-driver.example.com
        pool: kind-worker2
        request: request1
```

### What did you expect to happen?

For each config with the source as `FromClass`, I would expect the requests field to be set with the list of requests that are using the DeviceClass the config is coming from.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
kubectl apply -n blue -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceClass
metadata:
  name: deviceclass-0
spec:
  selectors:
  - cel:
      expression: device.driver == "resource-driver.example.com"
  config:
  - opaque:
      driver: resource-driver.example.com
      parameters:
        test: "example-0"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: DeviceClass
metadata:
  name: deviceclass-1
spec:
  selectors:
  - cel:
      expression: device.driver == "resource-driver.example.com"
  config:
  - opaque:
      driver: resource-driver.example.com
      parameters:
        test: "example-1"
---
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: my-resource-claim
spec:
  devices:
    requests:
    - exactly:
        allocationMode: ExactCount
        count: 1
        deviceClassName: deviceclass-0
      name: request0
    - exactly:
        allocationMode: ExactCount
        count: 1
        deviceClassName: deviceclass-1
      name: request1
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: demo
  labels:
    app: demo
spec:
  containers:
  - name: alpine
    image: alpine:latest
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    command:
    - sleep
    - infinity
  resourceClaims:
  - name: my-resource-claim
    resourceClaimTemplateName: my-resource-claim
EOF
```

```
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    metadata:
      creationTimestamp: null
      name: www
    spec:
      accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
      volumeMode: Filesystem
    status:
      phase: Pending
```

Deploy the same statefulset in a **1.34** version cluster.
You will get something like:

```

  annotations:
  creationTimestamp: "2025-10-23T10:14:03Z"

    whenScaled: Retain

  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 10
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  serviceName: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx

      containers:
      - image: k8s.gcr.io/nginx-slim:0.8
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        name: nginx
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
          protocol: TCP
        resources: {}
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
        terminationMessagePolicy: File
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst
      restartPolicy: Always
      schedulerName: default-scheduler
      securityContext: {}
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
  updateStrategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 0
    type: RollingUpdate

    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
```

No more **spec.template.metadata.creationTimestamp** field !
So upgrading cluster from 1.33 to 1.34 will trigger a rollout of pods managed by statefulset as the doc says about pod template.

"If you change the pod template for a workload resource, that resource needs to create replacement Pods that use the updated template."

> if you upgrade kubernetes version, it will recreate the pods, this is expected behavior

I think this is referring to the case where the control plane is only updated.

>if you upgrade kubernetes version, it will recreate the pods, this is expected behavior

I disagree. Control plane upgrade should NOT impact user workload especially for a change that is not marked as breaking change.

If I have a large cluster running some AI/ML training job using statefulset, upgrading to 1.34 means all my workload will be interrupted which is a real problem.

Thoughts? @liggitt @jpbetz @deads2k

I agree a control plane upgrade should not trigger workload rollouts. It looks like statefulsets use hashes of serialized statefulset template json as the indicator a change occurred, which is unfortunately fragile to any json-visible serialization changes under PodTemplate (as well as any field defaulting changes under pod template).

The creationTimestamp omitzero change presumed the field would always be populated server side, so would not change serialization in server responses, but that was only true for the root metadata.creationTimestamp.

Reverting the change would cause disruption in the opposite direction in 1.34 → 1.35 or 1.34.0 → 1.34.x upgrades, so I think we'll need to add a secondary check when statefulset is determining whether the latest revision is identical to the current state that checks if removal of `creationTimestamp:null` is needed to normalize for comparison.

xref previous issues with using exact json serialization / hashing for determining if a rollout or container restart was required:
* this issue for statefulset (fragile to json serialization and podtemplate field defaulting)
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/69445 (daemonset fragile to podtemplate defaulting, not fundamentally fixed in daemonset)
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/78633 (daemonset fragile to podtemplate defaulting, not fundamentally fixed in daemonset)
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/63814 (kubelet restarting containers based on json hash)
WIP fix in [REDACTED]
Fix in [REDACTED] is ready for review

title: when resuming a suspended kubernetes job, unhandled error of job controller occured in the log of kube-controller-manager pod
description:
### What happened? try to resume a suspended job, there are repeated error logs: error="syncing job: tracking status: adding uncounted pods to status: Job.batch is invalid: status.startTime: Required value: startTime cannot be removed for unsuspended job" as shown in the attached image. ### What did you expect to happen? no error occur in log of kube-controller-manager pod ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? 1. Create a kubernetes job. The job starts to run. 2. Suspend the job. The job is suspended. kubectl patch job/myjob --type=strategic --patch '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' 3. Interesting.

I also see this for [REDACTED]
cc @dejanzele @mimowo @tenzen-y
I am able to reproduce this on k8s 1.33.1 also.

Looks like this was added by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/e568a77a931a1cf4239a4a5fa43e2b05bad3abdf.

cc @mimowo 

When I did my testing I didn't see any functional issues with this though. Job still suspends and resumes.

Oh yes, this is a bug because when resuming the Job the Job controller would always update the status.startTime: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1058

To fix this I can see two options:
1. allow to update status.StartTime for unsuspended jobs
2. allow to update status.startTime for unsuspended jobs only when Job is resumed (so that isUpdated=true): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1047-L1048

I would suggest going for (2.) to be more strict.

cc @tenzen-y @atiratree @soltysh wdyt?
I already spoke with @mimowo , I'll look into it as part of the managed-by graduation to stable.
Wouldn't it be better if we set `.status.startTime` to nil every time `.spec.suspend` is set to true in the apiserver update logic? Or do you expect this to break anything?
I suppose we could also nil it a bit later in the controller when updating the `Suspended` condition to `True/JobSuspended`

Let me add for context that users of Kueue don't face this issue because Kueue clears status.startTime during the "stopJob" procedure: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/blob/main/pkg/controller/jobs/job/job_controller.go#L184-L192

> Wouldn't it be better if we set .status.startTime to nil every time .spec.suspend is set to true in the apiserver update logic? Or do you expect this to break anything?

This sounds like a good idea if this was written on day one, but since this is an old code of Job controller, I'm more tempted to adjust the new validation logic. 

IIRC it was considered some time ago, but we weren't sure about race conditions when user wants to quickly suspend / unsuspend. However, I don't see any catastrophic case anyway this is what we do in Kueue currently.

> I suppose we could also nil it a bit later in the controller when updating the Suspended condition to True/JobSuspended

^ should happen after the pods get deleted, but I guess a race can occur there as well. So to conclude we are weighing a race against a stricter Job API validation.

I guess we could also consider disabling setting suspend to true unless `True/JobSuspended` is observed, but that also seems limiting/problematic with existing clients.

> > I suppose we could also nil it a bit later in the controller when updating the Suspended condition to True/JobSuspended
> 
> ^ should happen after the pods get deleted, but I guess a race can occur there as well. So to conclude we are weighing a race against a stricter Job API validation.

I definitely agree there is room for improvement, but this is also touching a long existing behavior, so risky as a quick fix. 

So, I would rather consider introducing a new condition like `JobFullySuspended` to mark that all Pods are deleted.

Yeah, the "safe" path forward I see is: 
1. relax validation as a bugfix just when Resuming (option 2) from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134521#issuecomment-3414248956
2. consider improvements for "sequenced/strict" suspension, but that could be a separate "suspendMode: strict" maybe.  Then we could wait with validations until the suspention completes (pods are deleted, JobFullySuspended is reached, and startTime is cleared), before allowing to resume, but this would be a separate KEP likely with low ROI  because orchestrators like Kueue already do it.

> Yeah, the "safe" path forward I see is:
> 
> 1. relax validation as a bugfix just when Resuming (option 2) from [when resuming a suspended kubernetes job, unhandled error of job controller occured in the log of kube-controller-manager pod #134521 (comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134521#issuecomment-3414248956)

Then we could wait with validations until the suspention completes (pods are deleted, JobFullySuspended is reached, and startTime is cleared), before allowing to resume, but this would be a separate KEP likely with low ROI  because orchestrators like Kueue already do it.

IIUC, the above status validations were introduced to provide guide for external Job controllers leveraging managedBy field.
So, I'm ok with relaxing the validations with `allow to update status.startTime for unsuspended jobs only when Job is resumed (so that isUpdated=true):`.

As a long-term effort, we might want to introduce the processing state as a sibling of SuccessCriteriaMet and FailureTarget.
But, yes a long-term solution should be part of another KEP (issue).

> 1. relax validation as a bugfix just when Resuming (option 2) from [when resuming a suspended kubernetes job, unhandled error of job controller occured in the log of kube-controller-manager pod #134521 (comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134521#issuecomment-3414248956)

I'm even inclined to relax it such that it's allowed to clear the value when job is suspended.

title: No share ID in DRA kubelet plugin's API
description:
### What happened?

kubelet plugin API does not support ShareID information. The ShareID is an additional identifier to the device name which may be generated by DRAConsumableCapacity feature ( that is introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5104). 

The DRA driver which refers to this API for preparing resource needs to pass ShareID to CDI spec's device ID. Otherwise, the same node will fail to create a container according to the duplicate ID. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Pods can be successfully created when sharing the same device with DRAConsumableCapacity.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Enable DRAConsumableCapacity feature, Enable DRA driver with allowMultipleAllocations device, Create two pods allocating the same device.

### Anything else we need to know?

Without the change to k/k, a driver can have a workaround which wrap the plugin API appending with shareID and use it as a PreparedDevice.

From 
```go
type PreparedDevice struct {
	Device         DRADevice
	ContainerEdits *cdiapi.ContainerEdits
}
```
to
```go
type DRADevice struct {
	drapbv1.Device
	shareID *types.UID
}
type PreparedDevice struct {
	Device         DRADevice
	ContainerEdits *cdiapi.ContainerEdits
}
```
implemented code: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver/commit/939b1fdd3e3efec3a3c7ea758c394c5aabdfa422

However, it looks cleaner when we do that in the provided API.
The change needs at driver is only extending the CDI id with share id if not nil: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/dra-example-driver/commit/4a625314cb46ed38018d05e17a397420335277eb.

title: Kubelet rejects pod with "NodeAffinity failed" due to stale informer data
description:
#### What happened

This issue is similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/100467 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92067.

We have a controller that adds labels to a node after it starts up. It looks like there are cases where the scheduler is able to see the new node labels and schedule a pod, but the kubelet somehow doesn't see the new labels - it has stale data in its informer cache. Whatever the reason for the stale data, the result is that the kubelet rejects the pod with "NodeAffinity failed".

#### What did you expect to happen

Kubelet to be able to detect the new node labels and not reject the pod. 

The only reason that we need to keep the node affinity / node selector check in the kubelet is in case someone sets `nodeName` directly on the pod, so that it does not go through the scheduler, so we can't just remove enforcement on the node level.

The short-term fix would be for the kubelet to synchronously fetch the node object when (and only when) it sees these "NodeAffinity failed" errors and try again. To ensure we do not introduce additional heavy traffic when there many pods being scheduled at once, we will have to keep a new cache, separate from the informer cache. The logic would be like:
- Read the node object from the informer
- If we get a NodeAffinity failed error, read the node object from our new cache
- If we still get a NodeAffinity failed error, fetch the node object synchronously from the api server
The cache should be updated whenever we see a node object that is newer than the one we are currently storing - this can come from either the informer or from the synchronous fetch. 

Long term, maybe we can re-consider the flow for `nodeName`, or leverage something like [kubelet synchronous admission](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1O9rDeYhGWMbtg-DQmhqKvNsQSHWJSwvSEeNpXTKMvZg/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.6ggs708p6vvu) to keep the scheduler and kubelet coordinated. There are also some more general discussions about what to do when informer data is stale, maybe the outcomes there can help here.

#### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You'd probably have to restart kubelet a whole bunch of times, and have a controller that modifies the node labels whenever it restarts.

#### Environment
- Kubernetes version: The issue is reported as persistent from versions v1.18-v1.28+, and it is unlikely that it has been fixed in a more recent version.
- Cloud provider: GKE

comments.text:
For discussions on syncing informers.

> The logic would be like:
> 
> * Read the node object from the informer
> * If we get a NodeAffinity failed error, read the node object from our new cache
> * If we still get a NodeAffinity failed error, fetch the node object synchronously from the api server
>   The cache should be updated whenever we see a node object that is newer than the one we are currently storing - this can come from either the informer or from the synchronous fetch.

I think the first & second bullet can be combined. I'm picturing a cache object that looks something like this:

```go
type nodeCache struct {
	nodeName string
	nodeLister corelisters.NodeLister
	cachedNode *v1.Node
	client clientset.Interface
}

func (c *nodeCache) GetCache() *v1.Node {
	informerNode, _ := c.nodeLister.Get(c.nodeName)
	if c.cachedNode == nil || isNewer(informerNode, c.cachedNode) {
		return informerNode
	}
	return c.cachedNode
}

func (c *nodeCache) GetSync (*v1.Node, error) {
	node, err := c.client.CoreV1().Nodes().Get(context.Background(), c.nodeName, metav1.GetOptions{})
	if err != nil { return nil, err }
	c.cachedNode = node
	return node, nil
}
```

I'm just not sure how to do the `isNewer` check. I thought we weren't supposed to parse resourceVersion, but it looks like the [scheduler does it](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bbd859808d0cef566fbfc89639926b7cc50d9bd5/pkg/scheduler/util/assumecache/assume_cache.go#L236), so ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Then the steps look like:
1. Run the admission check using the node from `GetCache`
2. If there is a node affinity error, rerun the admission check using the node from `GetSync`

My preferred solution would be to just drop the affinity check from the Kubelet, but I don't think there's a backward compatible way we can do that. IMO the affinity check should just be a scheduling policy. Once the pod is scheduled to the node, the Kubelet shouldn't need to enforce it.

> My preferred solution would be to just drop the affinity check from the Kubelet, but I don't think there's a backward compatible way we can do that.

Yeah I'm not sure I understand what the affinity check in the kubelet is for. If someone is setting `nodeName` explicitly to bypass the scheduler, I could see the desired behavior as being to ignore node affinity (what is the purpose of setting `nodeName` to a node that's just going to reject the pod?). But I agree that it is too late to change this now.

> I'm just not sure how to do the `isNewer` check. I thought we weren't supposed to parse resourceVersion, but it looks like the [scheduler does it](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bbd859808d0cef566fbfc89639926b7cc50d9bd5/pkg/scheduler/util/assumecache/assume_cache.go#L236), so ¯_(ツ)_/¯

There's agreement on relaxing to let clients start comparing... specifics proposed in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5505

> My preferred solution would be to just drop the affinity check from the Kubelet, but I don't think there's a backward compatible way we can do that.

Yeah, historically labels/selectors and taints/tolerations have been used not only as scheduling directives but also as protection boundaries in combination with admission forcing / forbidding pods from selecting / tolerating specific nodes, so Kubelet also doing a check to refuse to run pods assigned to it but not matching its labels / tolerating its taints is something we can't drop.

title: [BUG] Server-Side-Apply: metadata.managedFields got wiped out by writing status to different version
description:
### What happened?

Writing to the status sub-resource of CRD somehow removes the managedFields if we use a different api version of the active storage.

### What did you expect to happen?

The managedFields should not be removed and should be kept. As `/status` endpoint by design should not be able to update the spec fields.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```console

Starting to serve on 127.0.0.1:8001
```

Hi, I’m looking into the behavior around managedFields handling for CRs.

In [this code reference](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ddd8e70b1e04ade755f3a37e008ff057ca2f1197/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/managedfields/internal/structuredmerge.go#L111) it seems that managedFields entries not matching the current CR version are removed. This appears to be the source of the issue I’m seeing. 

My question is whether this behavior was part of the original design intent. Since CRs are generally recommended to be managed by only one version of a controller, even during version upgrades, dropping old managedFields may not have any impact on the new controller. However, I’m not fully sure if this is expected or unintended.

If this was not the intended design, it seems we may need to consider updating the logic in [structured-merge-diff](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/structured-merge-diff/blob/d3e4dc6f630e155d2fbfdac465eb0da8a737245f/merge/update.go#L167-L204)

Would appreciate any clarification or guidance on this. Thanks! 🙏

@sbueringer

I think it's not intended that a write of one field manager with a different apiVersion than a previous write of another removes managedFields entries like this.

multiple apiVersions can in general co-exist: https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/periodic-cluster-api-e2e-main/1965249250098941952/artifacts/clusters/clusterctl-upgrade-management-k1xsji/resources/clusterctl-upgrade/Cluster/clusterctl-upgrade-workload-smu2jo.yaml

I think I’ve found the root cause. The issue lies in [this line](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/structured-merge-diff/blob/ccf7a061f165cd3feee92af191157c053154d8bc/merge/update.go#L104).When the object needs conversion and the request is targeting the status subresource, changes to spec should be discarded. versions[managerSet.APIVersion()] = compare.FilterFields(s.IgnoreFilter[version])

This way, the IgnoreFilter is still retrieved based on the API endpoint’s requested version.

description:
### What happened? There is a bug in `kubelet` `startupProbe` if sidecar container is configured. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.32/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go#L249 The worker's decision to continue (return true) or stop (return false) is based only on the pod's restart policy, not the containers (sidecar have restartPolicy:Always) This can lead to a racing condition if the sidecar container fails at the first time and prober incorrectly exits: If sidecar container restarted with no problem at second attempt, startupProbe will never run again. This leads kubelet to think the initContainer never successfully initialized. There is another bug in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go#L194 the probe can possibly get recreated here. However if there are more than one containers has startup probes, and the first container has a running probe, it will skip other containers (because of an early`return`). As a result, reproduction requires at least 2 startup probes. With the example in the "How to reproduce", the `main-container` is stuck in Initializing state. kubectl desribe pod

Image size: 2156518 bytes. Normal Pulling 19m (x2 over 19m) kubelet Pulling image "busybox" Normal Created 19m (x2 over 19m) kubelet Created container: buggy-init-container Normal Started 19m (x2 over 19m) kubelet Started container buggy-init-container Normal Pulled 19m kubelet Successfully pulled image "busybox" in 225ms (225ms including waiting). Image size: 2156518 bytes. ```
Timeline T=0s: The buggy-init-container starts. The prober creates a worker for it, which immediately begins its initialDelaySeconds: 10 wait. T=0.1s: The container's command runs, creates the /work/first_run_done file, and exits with code 1. The container is now in a Terminated state. T=0.1s to T=5s: The probe worker is still waiting for its initial delay to expire. It has not run a single probe. T=5s: The worker's delay is over, and it runs doProbe for the first time. It sees that the container is Terminated. The onHold flag is false because a probe has never completed. It proceeds to the check: if c.State.Running == nil. This is true. It executes the faulty return logic: return c.State.Terminated == nil || w.pod.Spec.RestartPolicy != v1.RestartPolicyNever. Since the pod's RestartPolicy is Never, this evaluates to false, and the probe worker terminates itself. Meanwhile: `kubelet` sees the terminated init container and, honoring its restartPolicy: Always, starts a new instance of it. The syncloop will attempt to recreate the probe. However due to the bug in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go#L194 , the loop will `return` early because the main container's probe already exists, it fails to check the initContainer's probe. The Kubelet sees a running container with a startup probe but not have a successful ran, assuming it's not ready. The main-container never starts. ### What did you expect to happen? startupProbe should honor the container's restartPolicy. The startupProbe should continue to probe even if the sidecar container has failed initially and restarts. Running as a sidecar." sleep infinity fi startupProbe: # This delay MUST be long enough for the first container instance # to start, run its command, and terminate. initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 2 failureThreshold: 3 # The probe command itself is irrelevant, as it will never be run # by the first worker. exec: command: ["/bin/true"] containers: - name: main-container image: registry.k8s.io/pause # Added a startupProbe to the main container. startupProbe: initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 5 exec: command: ["/bin/true"] ``` ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version

title: Deletion of csi-node-plugin Pod causes driver entry to be removed from CSINode object; kube-scheduler schedules more than driver's allocatable
description:
### What happened?

With @plkokanov we hit in our environments the following issue multiple times:
```
% k -n shoot--foo--bar describe po etcd-main-0

Events:
  Type     Reason              Age                 From                     Message
  ----     ------              ----                ----                     -------
  Warning  FailedAttachVolume  35s (x47 over 80m)  attachdetach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pv-shoot--shik--shak-1234" : rpc error: code = Internal desc = Attach volume /subscriptions/<omitted>/resourceGroups/shoot--shik--shak/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/pv-shoot--shik--shak-1234 to instance shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5 failed with Retriable: false, RetryAfter: 0s, HTTPStatusCode: 409, RawError: {\r
  "error": {\r
    "code": "OperationNotAllowed",\r
    "message": "The maximum number of data disks allowed to be attached to a VM of this size is 16.",\r
    "target": "dataDisks"\r
  }\r
}
```

When we checked, the CSINode object for the corresponding Node was reporting the correct volume attachment limit:
```
% k get csinode shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5 -o yaml

spec:
  drivers:
  # ...
  - allocatable:
      count: 16
    name: disk.csi.azure.com
    nodeID: shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5
    topologyKeys:
    - topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone
    - topology.kubernetes.io/zone
```

According to the Node status and according to the VM state in Azure, it had already 16 disks attached.
```
% k get no shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5 -o json | jq '.status.volumesAttached | length'
16

% az vm show -g shoot--shik--shak --name shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5 | jq '.storageProfile.dataDisks | length'
16
```

kube-scheduler wrongly sheduled a Pod with a volume to the `shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5` Node as the Node already had its volume attachments limit reached.

We found that this happens due to csi-node-plugin Pod deletion. On deletion of this Pod, we see that the driver section from the CSINode object is removed and it is added only when the new csi-node-plugin Pod starts.

The corresponding handling in kube-scheduler's NodeVolumeLimits plugin is: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a7242fcff768658019f878cb691583dcbcfefb2d/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodevolumelimits/csi.go#L197-L201

If we fail to fetch the limit from the CSINode object, kube-scheduler let's the Pod to be scheduled.

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-scheduler to do not schedule Pods with volumes to Nodes that already have their volume attachment limit reached.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

To reproduce the removal of the driver section after csi-node-plugin Pod deletion:

1. Start watching the CSINode object:
```
 k get csinode "$NODENAME" -w -o yaml > "~/csinode-$NODENAME.yaml"
```

2. In a new terminal window delete the csi-node-plugin Pod

3. Make sure that the CSINode object watch is as follows:
```yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: CSINode
metadata:
  name: node-1
spec:
  drivers:
  - allocatable:
      count: 8
    name: disk.csi.azure.com
    nodeID: node-1
    topologyKeys:
    - topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone
    - topology.kubernetes.io/zone
---
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: CSINode
metadata:
  name: node-1
spec:
  drivers: null
---
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: CSINode
metadata:
  name: node-1
spec:
  drivers:
  - allocatable:
      count: 8
    name: disk.csi.azure.com
    nodeID: node-1
    topologyKeys:
    - topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone
    - topology.kubernetes.io/zone
```

Note: The non-relevant fields are removed from the example output above.

You can see that until the new csi-node-plugin is scheduled and started, the CSINode object does not contain any information about the driver. We see that during that time kube-scheduler schedules new Pods with volumes to that Node.
The kube-scheduler plugin for respecting the Node volume limit is: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a7242fcff768658019f878cb691583dcbcfefb2d/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodevolumelimits/csi.go

### Anything else we need to know?

We use VPA to scale the csi-node-plugin Pod. That's why it can be evicted and restarted.

```console
$ kubectl version

Server Version: v1.29.4
```

</details>

<details>
Azure and AWS
</details>

```console
# On Linux:
$ cat /etc/os-release
# paste output here
$ uname -a
# paste output here

# On Windows:
C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture
# paste output here
```


title: Overaggressive Routes Controller
description:
**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:


**What happened**:
`Route controller` is unnecessary too aggressive. The [current control loop](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/route/route_controller.go#L115) loops through the node list every `10s`. Each node will generate a `GET` call to cloud resource manager (ARM in case of `azure`) to assert the route existence, This quickly burns through the quota afforded to each subscription (the umbrella concept used by `azure` to manage multiple clusters/ resource groups) by the underlaying cloud. Nodes does not change their own ip that frequent on `azure` or any cloud/om-prem deployment for that matter. Once the cluster burns through the quota its control plane will become practically unusable until quota refill, refresh or manual shutdown/start of controller to slow down the calls.

Setting it to higher period is not the best solution, since we need the route controller to kick in in case of scale up/down or the unlikely case of node changing IPs. 

**What you expected to happen**:
`Route Controller` must generate the smallest possible of cloud calls. Ideally, only when needed. And must be reasonably fast in reaction to changing state such as `new nodes`, `deleted nodes`, or changing `node ip`  

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Either run many small clusters (10 X 20 nodes) in the same `azure` subscription (or the equivalent concept on different environments), Or run one large cluster (400++ node). The controller will quickly log `HTTP 429` (in `azure` case) throttling errors 

**Proposed Solution**
change `Route Controller` implementation to `Service Controller` [like](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/service/service_controller.go#L136) implementation using `shared informer`. Because `node` object gets frequently updated (example node status updates) the controller should maintain an in memory cache of `node:ip` and should only call out the `cloud provider` when the node is new or its ip has changed. We can extend this by a `full sync` every long period just in case of faulty state drifts.

**Anything else we need to know?**:
N/A 

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): *
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: `azure` et al
- OS (e.g. from /etc/os-release): *
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): *

- Others:*

title: SELinux warning controller reports conflicts for finished Pods
description:
### What happened?

The SELinux warning controller emits metrics + events when two pods that have different SELinux labels and share the same volume. This may not be supported when SELinuxMount feature gets GA. See the [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-storage/1710-selinux-relabeling).

However, the controller reports these conflicting SELinux labels also for Pods in Failed or Succeeded phase. Kubelet is umounting volumes from these pods by default, so they cannot conflict with any other volume.

### What did you expect to happen?

The controller should ignore Succeeded and Failed pods.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run a pod that uses a PVC with SELinux label `s0:c0,c1` to completion (either Succeeded or Failed). Run a second pod that uses the same volume and has label `s0:c98,c99`. The controller now emits an event that these pods are conflicting. But the first one is finished and its volumes are unmounted, so they don't really conflict.

title: E2e test "should preempt lower priority pods using ReadWriteOncePod volumes" flakes
description:
### What happened?

We observed the e2e test `External Storage [Driver: disk.csi.azure.com] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] read-write-once-pod [MinimumKubeletVersion:1.27] should preempt lower priority pods using ReadWriteOncePod volumes` causes flakes in other e2e tests in a downstream CI job with Azure Disk CSI driver.

[The test](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4e94e70dcad423e9f59f12ac5a048d2137d20e86/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/readwriteoncepod.go#L133) runs a default (low-prio) pod1 with a `ReadWriteOncePod` volume and then starts a high prio pod2 that tries to use the same volume. To run pod2, the scheduler has to evict pod1 to make the RWOP volume "free" for pod2. That works great, however, it may evict also pods of other e2e tests that run with the default priority.

What happened on a busy clusters, with all nodes at their attachment limit.

1. pod1 runs, pod2 is created.
2. The scheduler evicts pod1. That frees the RWOP volume and it also frees the last attachment slot on the node.
3. Some other e2e tests creates a Pod and scheduler puts it on the node, taking the last attachment slot.
4. The scheduler schedules pod2 agaian and it sees there is no node with a free attachment slot -> new round of eviction, now evicting a pod of unrelated e2e tests. The unrelated test will fail.  

We observed it with Azure, which can attach only 8 disks on the cheaper nodes, so it's more reproducible there.

### What did you expect to happen?

The preemption test should not affect other e2e tests

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above

title: drain daemonSetFilter does not use drain helper context
description:
### What happened?

In the `k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/drain` package, the daemonset filter uses `context.TODO()` instead of the drain helper's context. [Source code permalink](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/61c629cc57649bf0ce2378903027c83939d84109/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/drain/filters.go#L196).

This has implications for time outs and for logging, where any loggers passed as part of the context will be used for all calls except this one.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected this function to use the context included in the Helper struct if available via the `getContext` method

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

n/a, although you will notice the logging effect if you pass a `logr.Discard()` to the `Helper`. When running `RunNodeDrain` on a high verbosity, you will see many logs printed from the DaemonSet get call

_No response_

title: Conntrack entries cleanup efficiency degradation ( > 1.32 ) causing rule synchronization delays and service access issues
description:
### What happened? After Kubernetes v1.32, kube-proxy's conntrack cleanup mechanism changed from batch deletion using `conntrack -D `command to individual entry deletion via netlink API. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127318 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126130 although some bugfix and improvement have been done in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129982 1.31: 1.32 or higher: This change significantly reduced cleanup efficiency, causing severe service synchronization delays when updating UDP related svc/ep in high dns-resolve QPS scenarios. ### What did you expect to happen? Conntrack entries should be cleaned up efficiently without blocking syncProxyRules, ensuring timely service rule synchronization even if updating UDP related svc/ep frequently. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? 1. Test Environment: kube-proxy mode: iptables (as in ipvs, we have `net.ipv4.vs.expire_nodest_conn = 1` mechanism, if we disable it manually, we can still reproduce this problem easily.) 10 pod (name: dns-query); each pod doing DNS query once per sec, with 1000 goroutines. generating ~10,000 QPS DNS requests at node level. no dns cache. 2. Wait for conntrack entries to accumulate: ``` # conntrack -Ln -p udp | wc -l conntrack v1.4.4 (conntrack-tools): 282121 flow entries have been shown. 282121 ``` 3. Trigger conntrack cleanup by rolling CoreDNS pods to generate new endpoints 4. Observe the cleanup duration and service availability Observed Impact on v1.33: Conntrack cleanup time in syncProxyRules: ``` I1114 07:15:31.456513 1 cleanup.go:51] "Started to reconcile conntrack entries" ipFamily="IPv4" I1114 07:22:59.255367 1 cleanup.go:149] "Finished reconciling conntrack entries" ipFamily="IPv4" entriesDeleted=133750 took="7m27.798843433s" ``` During this 7+ minute cleanup period, IF CoreDNS pods were rolled again, rules could not be synchronized in time, causing complete DNS resolution failures in over. Comparison with v1.31: Same scenario with v1.31 using batch deletion: ``` I1114 07:55:25.395120 1 conntrack.go:83] "Clearing conntrack entries" parameters=["-D","--orig-dst","192.168.0.10","--dst-nat","10.0.0.223","-p","udp"] I1114 07:55:26.102196 1 conntrack.go:88] "Conntrack entries deleted" output=< udp 17 113 src=conntrack v1.4.7 (conntrack-tools): 140366 flow entries have been deleted. ``` Cleanup completed in ~0.7 seconds vs 7+ minutes in v1.33, when cleaning up ~140k conntrack flows. ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version
Kubernetes version: v1.33 (issue present), v1.31 (working correctly)
### Cloud provider
Alibaba Cloud ACK
### OS version
```console # On Linux: $ cat /etc/os-release # paste output here $ uname -a # paste output here # On Windows: C:\> wmic os get Caption, Version, BuildNumber, OSArchitecture # paste output here ```

```
[root@xxx:/paasdata/op-log/k8s]$ curl 10.254.223.183:80
curl: (7) Failed to connect to 10.254.223.183 port 80: Connection refused

-A KUBE-SERVICES -d 10.254.223.183/32 -p tcp -m comment --comment "default/svc-clusterip-deploy:web has no endpoints" -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
```

### What did you expect to happen?

iptables rules is normal.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The CNI plugin must support assigning static IPs to pods of the deployment type. 

When the node hosting the pod powers down, the pod is evicted. However, because the kubelet fails to clean up, the pod remains in a terminating state while the newly created pod enters a running state. 

Both pods share the same IP address.

### Anything else we need to know?

in k8s1.22, two pods with same ip will cause endpointslices only have the terminating endpont sometimes, because two endpoint have same hash key.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bc4763cbf8b9e6adfbc07bb3194509b187b0b901/pkg/controller/util/endpointslice/endpointset.go#L49-L54

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bc4763cbf8b9e6adfbc07bb3194509b187b0b901/pkg/controller/util/endpointslice/endpointset.go#L35-L43

for endpointslices with one terminating endpoint, kube-proxy will not generate iptables rules. we modify Insert function to solve the replace problem, but it not take affect in k8s 1.28 and newer version due to #115907.
```
func (s EndpointSet) Insert(items ...*discovery.Endpoint) EndpointSet {
	for _, item := range items {
		// 1. two pods with same pod ip, pod1 is running, pod2 is terminating
		// 2. if pod1 already insert into EndpointSet, pod2 should not override pod1
		if _, ok := s[hashEndpoint(item)]; ok {
			if *item.Conditions.Terminating || *item.Conditions.Ready == false {
				continue
			}
		}

		s[hashEndpoint(item)] = item
	}
	return s
}
```

after pr #115907 merged, two pods with same ip, endpointslices will have two endpoint, kube-proxy handle the endpointslice,  function addEndpoints will only return one endpoint. it maybe the terminating pod, and kube-proxy will not generate iptables rules also.

title: PodAffinity's QHint misses the scenario with existing pods' anti-affinity
description:
### What happened?

The inter-pod affinity plugin is filtering out the nodes that have running pods with pod-anti-affinity that hates the pod being scheduled.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/849a82b727b1cc1e77b58149b3cacbfa5ada30fd/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L427-L429

However PodAffinity's QHint only checks if a pending pod's anti-affinity hates a deleted pod, and doesn't check if a deleted pod's anti-affinity hates a pending pod.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/849a82b727b1cc1e77b58149b3cacbfa5ada30fd/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/plugin.go#L202-L207 

It causes the inter-pod affinity plugin to miss the pod/delete events that could make pending pods schedulable.

### What did you expect to happen?

PodAffinity's QHint checks _both_ if a pending pod's anti-affinity hates a deleted pod _and_ if a deleted pod's anti-affinity hates a pending pod.

comments.text: Are you trying to mutate that with an apply patch? If so, I think that is actually an invalid pod for apply

I did use apply on it for testing. It warned but applied fine without the MAP. With the MAP, its rejected.

Noticed because we have some older gitlab-runners in some places, and they only fairly recently fixed an issue with duplicate env vars.

Here's an example MAP we are using, v1alpha1 since we are still running 1.33:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: MutatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: seccomp-profile-default
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  reinvocationPolicy: IfNeeded
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   [""]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE"]
      resources:   ["pods"]
  matchConditions:
  - name: host-users-not-false
    expression: "!has(object.spec.hostUsers) || object.spec.hostUsers != false"
  mutations:
  - patchType: "ApplyConfiguration"
    applyConfiguration:
      expression: >
        Object{
          spec: Object.spec{
            securityContext: Object.spec.securityContext{
              seccompProfile: Object.spec.securityContext.seccompProfile{
                type: "RuntimeDefault"
              }
            }
          }
        }
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: MutatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: seccomp-profile-default-user-tenant
spec:
  policyName: seccomp-profile-default
  matchResources:
    namespaceSelector:
      matchExpressions:
        - key: user-tenant
          operator: Exists
```

I will say that I just saw another ticket about duplicate environment variables out here https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/31529 that shows server side apply blocks duplicate environment variables even without using Mutating Admission Policies.  I was able to test this on our cluster and `kubectl create` and `kubectl apply --server-side=false` print a warning about duplicate environment variables but the pod is accepted by the apiserver.  `kubectl apply --server-side` refuses the pod with an error.  I've included my sample pod below and the output for commands for namespaces not covered by MAP and covered by MAP.

Sample Pod:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: hello-world
spec:
  containers:
  - name: hello-world-container
    image: nginx:latest
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80
    env:
    - name: test
      value: a
    - name: test
      value: b
```

`kubectl create` and `kubectl apply --server-side=false` warning on a namespace without the policy:

```
Warning: spec.containers[0].env[1]: hides previous definition of "test", which may be dropped when using apply
pod/hello-world created
```

`kubectl apply --server-side` error on a namespace with and without the policy:

```
Error from server: failed to create typed patch object (default/hello-world; /v1, Kind=Pod): .spec.containers[name="hello-world-container"].env: duplicate entries for key [name="test"]
```

`kubectl create` and `kubectl apply --server-side=false` error on a namespace with the policy:

```
The pods "hello-world" is invalid: : policy 'seccomp-profile-default' with binding 'seccomp-profile-default-user-tenant' denied request: error applying patch: failed to convert original object to typed object: .spec.containers[name="hello-world-container"].env: duplicate entries for key [name="test"]
```

Thanks for reporting this.

**Root Cause**
The issue stems from how Mutating Admission Policy (MAP) using `ApplyConfiguration` processes existing objects. It relies on the Structured Merge Diff (SMD) library to apply changes. By default, SMD enforces strict schema validation, which explicitly disallows duplicate entries in lists defined as associative maps (like the `env` list in Pod specs, which uses [name](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ec1bf8a4f3a5f054065225dc8275c66b93310d17/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L2968-L2970) as a key).

While Kubernetes legacy validation is permissive and allows these duplicates (only issuing a warning), the strict SMD conversion used by MAP rejects the object before the mutation can be applied, resulting in the `failed to convert original object to typed object` error.

**Workaround**
As an immediate workaround, you can try using `JSONPatch` mutations instead of `ApplyConfiguration`. JSON Patch operates independently of the Structured Merge Diff schema enforcement used here and should effectively bypass this specific validation error on the original object.

**Fix**
This issue is addressed in [REDACTED] That PR updates the internal logic to explicitly allow duplicates when processing the original object, ensuring that MAP can handle existing workloads with these legacy configurations without crashing.

The fix aligns how Mutation admission policy and Server side apply handle cases where duplicates are present in the persisted object.  

@liggitt I think we should merge the fix in the 1.35 release. What do you think?

title: kubelet_volume_stats_* metrics not available in 1.34
description:

When using Kubernetes version 1.34 `kubelet_volume_stats_*` metrics such as `kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes` are no longer present in `kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$NODE/proxy/metrics"`.

I know that they are in Alpha state and Alpha metrics do not come with any guarantees, but since they are still [documented](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/#list-of-alpha-kubernetes-metrics) I expect them to be visible. If this change was intended, it doesn't seem to be documented.

I was not able to correlate this with anything mentioned in [CHANGELOG-1.34.md](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-1.34.md).

title: GatedPods metric negative
description:
### What happened?

Kube-Scheduler currently provides a PreEnqueue plugin that prevents pods from entering ActiveQ or BackoffQ before they meet the scheduling requirements. This plugin is currently used to support the SchedulingGate feature. However, the Kube-Scheduler implementation does not seem to account for the possibility of pods becoming Gated from non-Gated state, resulting in some anomalies in GatedPods metrics. 

The problematic code is as follows. When GatedBefore is false and PreEnqueue returns a failure, a pod is generated with the metric "UnschedulablePods" but the actual podInfo.Gated = true. When this pod is deleted, the Gated metric may become negative.

```go
func (p *PriorityQueue) moveToActiveQ(logger klog.Logger, pInfo *framework.QueuedPodInfo, event string) bool {
	gatedBefore := pInfo.Gated()
	// If SchedulerPopFromBackoffQ feature gate is enabled,
	// PreEnqueue plugins were called when the pod was added to the backoffQ.
	// Don't need to repeat it here when the pod is directly moved from the backoffQ.
	if !p.isPopFromBackoffQEnabled || event != framework.BackoffComplete {
		p.runPreEnqueuePlugins(context.Background(), pInfo)
	}

	added := false
	p.activeQ.underLock(func(unlockedActiveQ unlockedActiveQueuer) {
		if pInfo.Gated() {
			// Add the Pod to unschedulablePods if it's not passing PreEnqueuePlugins.
			if unlockedActiveQ.has(pInfo) {
				return
			}
			if p.backoffQ.has(pInfo) {
				return
			}
			if p.unschedulablePods.get(pInfo.Pod) != nil {
				return
			}
			p.unschedulablePods.addOrUpdate(pInfo, event)
			logger.V(5).Info("Pod moved to an internal scheduling queue, because the pod is gated", "pod", klog.KObj(pInfo.Pod), "event", event, "queue", unschedulableQ)
			return
		}
		if pInfo.InitialAttemptTimestamp == nil {
			now := p.clock.Now()
			pInfo.InitialAttemptTimestamp = &now
		}

		unlockedActiveQ.add(pInfo, event)
		added = true

		p.unschedulablePods.delete(pInfo.Pod, gatedBefore)
		p.backoffQ.delete(pInfo)
		logger.V(5).Info("Pod moved to an internal scheduling queue", "pod", klog.KObj(pInfo.Pod), "event", event, "queue", activeQ)
		if event == framework.EventUnscheduledPodAdd.Label() || event == framework.EventUnscheduledPodUpdate.Label() {
			p.AddNominatedPod(logger, pInfo.PodInfo, nil)
		}
	})
	return added
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

GatedPods Metric should be correct!

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Implement a custom PreEnqueue Plugin, attempting to update it to make it gated from ungated, then delete it.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: Kubelet certificate not reloaded after replacement
description:
### What happened?

I am running the kubelet with a custom TLS certificate, using:

```yaml
tlsCertFile: /etc/kubernetes/pki/kubelet.crt
tlsPrivateKeyFile: /etc/kubernetes/pki/kubelet.key
```

I am automatically rotating this certificate using OpenBao. After some time, I see an error about an expired certificate:

```
> kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-apiserver-node-0 
Error from server: Get "https://172.29.0.2:10250/containerLogs/kube-system/kube-apiserver-node-0/kube-apiserver": tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2025-07-16T19:47:40Z is after 2025-06-30T23:08:51Z
```

However, the certificate on disk is still valid:

```
# openssl x509 -noout -text < /etc/kubernetes/pki/kubelet.crt 
Certificate:
    Data:
        Version: 3 (0x2)
        Serial Number:
            7a:7a:b8:8e:ca:dc:61:19:f8:a7:07:ce:35:1a:ed:86:79:e8:21:bb
        Signature Algorithm: ecdsa-with-SHA384
        Issuer: CN = Cerai kubelet CA
        Validity
            Not Before: Jul 13 19:54:43 2025 GMT
            Not After : Jul 20 19:55:13 2025 GMT
        Subject: CN = kubelet
```

It seems the kubelet is not reloading the changed certificate. Running `systemctl restart kubelet` fixes the issue temporarily (until the certificate expires again).

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect the kubelet to function correctly, as long as the certificate on disk is valid.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I haven't tested this reproducer yet, I will do that tomorrow. But I think the following should be sufficient:

1. Start the kubelet with `tlsCertFile`
3. Overwrite the certificate on-disk with a new certificate
4. Observe that the kubelet is still using the old certificate

### Anything else we need to know?

I'm happy to work on a fix for this.

> /triage accepted

@aramase curious if you envision this as a KEP? Or just a feature PR?

👋 
Hey, sorry if I'm missing something, but I would expect kubelet to reload certificates without need of a restart after https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124574 ?

@SergeyKanzhelev - I'm not very familiar with how the kubelet and this serverCertificateManager work exactly but, from a node that's running k8s 1.33, I'm able to see that the original (and expired) certificate is shown if I use `openssl` without passing in `-servername`:

```
# openssl s_client -CAfile /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-ca.pem -connect 10.128.34.82:10250 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
notBefore=Jul 28 18:07:05 2025 GMT
notAfter=Aug  4 13:18:51 2025 GMT
```

but then, I get the renewed certificate with:
```
# openssl s_client -CAfile /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-ca.pem -servername 10.128.34.150 -connect 10.128.34.82:10250 </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
notBefore=Aug  6 20:40:38 2025 GMT
notAfter=Aug 13 17:34:55 2025 GMT
```

Compared to what's on disk:
```
# openssl x509 -startdate -enddate -noout -in /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-cert.pem
notBefore=Aug  6 20:40:38 2025 GMT
notAfter=Aug 13 17:34:55 2025 GMT
```

In this case, we can no longer use `kubectl logs` or `kubectl exec` against pods on this node as they fail with:
```
 tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid: current time 2025-08-07T21:35:44Z is after 2025-08-04T13:18:51Z
```

My theory is that somewhere the original cert is still getting held in memory and being returned for non-SNI requests whereas the correctly reloaded cert is returned for SNI requests.

@SergeyKanzhelev sorry, I missed the question directed at me. I'm running 1.33.3 and haven't set any feature gates manually, so `ReloadKubeletServerCertificateFile` should be defaulting to enabled.

I can also confirm @jaredledvina's report - if I specify `-servername $NODE_IP`, `openssl s_client` shows the updated certificate. Without this flag, it shows the expired cert (and `kubectl logs` doesn't work, so presumably that is not sending SNI internally).

I think I've figured this out - the `tls.Config.getCertificate` only calls `tls.Config.GetCertificate` if `clientHello.ServerName` is set or `tls.Config.Certificates` is empty: https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.25.0:src/crypto/tls/common.go;l=1267-1273;drc=3a3c006ac07886aa923a8aad0a4b3ed954640973

~However, the kubelet initialization code sets `tls.Config.Certificates` ([here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f47e9696d7237f1011d23c9b55f6947e60526179/cmd/kubelet/app/server.go#L1166-L1173)), but then doesn't unset this when populating `tls.Config.GetCertificate` [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f47e9696d7237f1011d23c9b55f6947e60526179/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L912-L919). So if we don't use SNI, we get the stale certificate that was loaded on initialization.~

Ok, not quite - we call `http.Server.ListenAndServeTLS`, passing in the `TLSOptions.CertFile` and `.KeyFile`. This then populates `http.Server.TLSConfig.Certificates` [here](https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.25.0:src/net/http/server.go;l=3522-3529;drc=3a3c006ac07886aa923a8aad0a4b3ed954640973). So I think the correct thing is still to unset `TLSOptions.CertFile` and `.KeyFile` when filling in `.GetCertificate`.

Go's TLS client doesn't set SNI when connecting to an IP address, see [here](https://cs.opensource.google/go/go/+/refs/tags/go1.25.0:src/crypto/tls/handshake_client.go;l=1316-1318;drc=3a3c006ac07886aa923a8aad0a4b3ed954640973).

I'm happy to make a PR fixing this, but need to think about a better way to test this.

I have a fix, working on a way to test this (but might need some help there).

@SergeyKanzhelev should this be re-classified as a bug, since certificate reloading _should_ work as with #124574?
was it never worked? Or there is a special conditions for this? I am trying to understand if the priority wise and severity wise we need to cherry-pick to previous versions.

> was it never worked? Or there is a special conditions for this?

As far as I understand, the conditions required are that:

1. the kubelet is using externally provided certificates (via `tlsCertFile` and `tlsPrivateKeyFile` kubelet options) 
2. the the apiserver tries to connect to the kubelet by IP address

I'm not sure what controls (2). I _think_ this depends on the flag `--kubelet-preferred-address-types` which defaults to `Hostname,InternalDNS,InternalIP,ExternalDNS,ExternalIP`, and what kind of address the node has configured in `status.addresses`, see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ef4add4509a479dab1f34369dacb7e65a3fa2e81/pkg/kubelet/client/kubelet_client.go#L161-L213).

If that is correct, then it only affects clusters where `InternalIP` or `ExternalIP` are the preferred connection type. The cluster where I see this issue does have `--kubelet-preferred-address-types=InternalIP,...`. Unfortunately, I don't have any cluster where I set `tlsCertFile` and don't override `--kubelet-preferred-address-types`, so I'm not 100% sure if that would trigger the issue.
ok, so it is not a regression and is not warranting the backport. Thank you for finding the issue and a PR.

For our setup, we use the default `--kubelet-preferred-address-types`.
(also, our internal certificate primarily use DNS name in the cert SAN. Kubelet cert doesn't use IP address in the cert SAN).

From the log, the api-server makes requests as `https://node-dns-name:20250/containerLogs/...` and and don't encounter this issue.
Maybe some of those clarifications can be added to the release notes in [REDACTED] So it is not as wide as "general certificate reload issue".
My set up has  --kubelet-preferred-address-types=InternalIP,ExternalIP,Hostname . Is this also can cause cert reload issue ?

> My set up has --kubelet-preferred-address-types=InternalIP,ExternalIP,Hostname . Is this also can cause cert reload issue ?

Yes, this issue can happen for the configuration that use "IP based" connection to Kubelet.

title: kube-scheduler does not consider hostPort ports used by initContainers when scheduling
description:
### What happened?

When running two pods that both use hostNetwork and have sidecar initContainers (restartPolicy: Always) using the same port, kube-scheduler allows the pods to be scheduled on the same node.

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-scheduler does not schedule these two pods on the same node, following the behavior for pods using hostNetwork ports via a main container.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a kind cluster: `kind create cluster`.  The cluster only has one node.
2. Apply p1:
   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: p1
   spec:              
     hostNetwork: true
     dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
     initContainers:
     - name: init
       restartPolicy: Always    
       image: python:3.12                                                                                                                                                                                                            
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - python -m http.server 8081
       ports:
       - containerPort: 8081
     containers:
     - name: main
       image: python:3.12
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - sleep 10000
   ```
3. Apply p2:
   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: p2
   spec:
     hostNetwork: true
     dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
     initContainers:
     - name: init
       restartPolicy: Always    
       image: python:3.12                                                                                                                                                                                                            
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - python -m http.server 8081
       ports:
       - containerPort: 8081
     containers:
     - name: main
       image: python:3.12
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - sleep 10000
   ```
4. p2 is scheduled (and crashing because p1 is already using the port).

### Anything else we need to know?

kube-scheduler already accounts for hostNetwork ports used by main containers.  For example:

1. Create a kind cluster: `kind create cluster`.  The cluster only has one node.
2. Apply p1:
   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: p1
   spec:              
     hostNetwork: true
     dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
     containers:
     - name: main
       image: python:3.12
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - python -m http.server 8081
       ports:
       - containerPort: 8081
   ```
3. Apply p2:
   ```
   apiVersion: v1
   kind: Pod
   metadata:
     name: p2
   spec:
     hostNetwork: true
     dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet
     containers:
     - name: main
       image: python:3.12
       command:
       - /bin/bash
       - -c
       - python -m http.server 8081

       - containerPort: 8081
   ```

title: VolumeAttachment is not deleted when the CSI plugin change from requiring attach to not requiring attach
description:
### What happened?

After [volumeAttacher.Attach](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.32.0/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L271) executes successfully, the volumeattachment will be created. At this point, if CSI's ATTACHREQUIRED changes from true to false, it will cause [MarkVolumeAsAttached](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.32.0/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L301) to fail.
 And the volume will be removed from the [dsw](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.32.0/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/populator/desired_state_of_world_populator.go#L166), leaving the VolumeAttachment stranded without being properly cleaned up.

### What did you expect to happen?

volumeattachment can be cleaned up.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Install xsky-nfs-csi (other CSI drivers should be able to reproduce this) and set attachRequired to true
2. Create PVC and pod using the CSI
3. Keep querying volumeattachment using 'kubectl get volumeattachment'. As soon as the volumeattachment appears, immediately uninstall the CSI driver, then reinstall it with attachRequired set to false
4. After waiting for some time, query volumeattachment again and find that the volumeattachment still hasn't been deleted

### Anything else we need to know?

[operation_generator.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.32.0/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L301-L307)
I think we should add error handling here to mark the volume as "Uncertain", so the volume can be added to asw, allowing the next retry to successfully remove the VolumeAttachment.
I have tested that this can solve the problem. If confirmed this is an issue, I will submit a PR

IIUC, this issue may be related to `enqueueSSAfter` twice when we reconcile the StatefulSet.
First,
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22243bcfc657122f91db4a4547608d942e08ac12/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set.go#L223-L238

and then
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/22243bcfc657122f91db4a4547608d942e08ac12/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set.go#L487-L489

It will update the workqueue event (double the delay time) after call `enqueueSSAfter` the second time.
similar issue to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108266#issuecomment-1302639795

If folks agree that the current implementation is completely deterministically "in practice, StatefulSets treat minReadySeconds as if it is double the value provided", perhaps a note could at least be added to the docs about this for now?

(But maybe it's not deterministic... I don't understand this well enough to tell. Like maybe if the controller restarts then it might check availability before the second minReadySeconds period?)

We need a proper fix instead of changing the API/documentation. I think I can write an alternative fix to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/113605 that does not depend on the changes to the queue implementation.
I certainly would like this to be fixed too, but couldn't a short-term warning noting that a bug exists be better than nothing?

I don't think it is a good idea to document bugs as a standard behavior. We should strive to be compliant with the API: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset/#minimum-ready-seconds
There is a work around that we will not enqueue the item when we know that this item has existed in workqueue. But this has a prerequisite that the workqueue supports query operations.
